title: Prove omp find tool: ranks files/passages for a search
description:

SURFACE: find - omp judge role typesafe/jev-latest. Current evidence: jev-f1le verified: follow-through 331/444 (74.5%), top-3 305/331 (92%), bar >= grep and top-3 >= 60% PASS.
WHAT: produce a measured outcome for this surface on real traffic or a controlled live experiment you build (fresh omp sessions, real prompts or commands cut from session files). If the data does not exist, create it. UNMEASURED / NOT_RUN is never an acceptable close.
ACCEPTANCE: (1) a bar committed in a bead comment BEFORE outcome data is read; (2) the number with its denominator and a 95% interval where it is a rate; (3) spend stated; (4) a planted negative; (5) on a FAIL, LOSS DEPTH (autopsy, 3 one-variable hypotheses, dev replay, one held-out retest) before parking; (6) update work/jev-inventory/expected.json with the new verdict and re-bless the golden. A non-author verifies and closes.
NO-CLAIM: whatever the bar does not cover.

title: pre-commit AUTOFIX_REFUSED tells agents to run autofix --staged, which rewrites and re-stages sibling files: 3 sweeps on 2026-09-25
description:
WHAT: githooks/pre-commit lane 2 (lines 131-135) prints the remedy '<autofix> --staged --repo <repo>' then 'git add -- <the rewritten paths>'. Change it to print the exact paths of THIS commit: inside the hook, git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR reads the commit's own index (under git commit --only <paths> that is a temporary index holding only those paths), so the remedy becomes '<autofix> --repo <repo> -- <those paths>' and 'git add -- <those paths>'. autofix-precommit.sh already takes explicit files (its safety contract item 1: only files in argv). Add a gate witness: a scratch repo where a sibling file is staged and unclean, a path-limited commit of another unclean file is refused, and the printed remedy names only the committing path.

WHY: run manually, 'autofix --staged' uses the real shared index, so it reformats every staged file including other panes' work, and the agent then re-stages what it lists. Measured 2026-09-25: 792b309 (pane 2, Jericho Detective rows) carried pane 4's notes/deep/next-gen/pokeagent-emerald-scope.md; SkillCensus's fixer run reformatted pane 3's staged work/poke-jev/test_player.py before 3b8cf17; c60edae was reported as a third and then corrected. AGENTS.md 'save only your work' is broken by our own hook text.

ACCEPTANCE: githooks/* is a kit-guard gate path, so the edit runs in a KIT_GATE_EDIT=1 session. Witness red on the old text (names a sibling or says --staged), green on the new; foundation/gates.sh --portable and --selftest --portable exit 0; one real path-limited commit with a deliberately unclean own file shows the new remedy. Non-author check by a pane that did not edit.
close_reason: Non-author AmberWillow: holds at 6b104f5 (CI 36106761691 green). My scratch witness /tmp/verify-06w2.sh (jev hooks via git archive; sibling.py unclean and staged, own.py unclean, git commit --only -- own.py): old hook 6b104f5^ prints 'autofix-precommit.sh --staged --repo ...'; new hook prints '... --repo <repo> -- own.py' and 'git add -- own.py', 0 mentions of sibling.py or --staged. Running the new remedy fixed own.py and left sibling.py byte-identical.

comments.author: josh
comments.text: IMPLEMENTED 6b104f5 (pushed). RED before hook change: witness FAIL autofix trigger: path-limited remedy; old refusal printed autofix-precommit.sh --staged --repo ... and git add -- <the rewritten paths> despite sibling.py staged. GREEN after change: witness PASS autofix trigger: remedy names own.py, not staged sibling.py or --staged; 60-staged-deletion-lane: pre-commit wrapper proven — 3 triggers + 6 satisfying witnesses. bash foundation/gates.sh --portable -> gates: ALL GREEN (exit 0); bash foundation/gates.sh --selftest --portable -> gates: ALL GREEN (exit 0). title: Observability that closes itself: per-surface heartbeat, auto-switch-off on anomaly
description:
WHAT: every live surface declares its expected rows per eligible host event (tool results, turns; a CI fitted on 7 d of logs) and an error-rate ceiling; the watcher checks hourly, pages the owner, and on a sustained anomaly puts that surface into its OFF state (per the switch registry's polarity) with the reason; it runs as a supervised launchd service with a liveness row; restore goes through a log-only probe window. WHY: skill veto logged allow with empty scores, screens capped silently, the gate hook stopped loading: each found by a human hours later. ACCEPTANCE: planted silent surface and planted error spike each trip alarm + off-switch within one check; healthy surfaces stay on; an idle fleet (zero host traffic) trips nothing.

SUPERSEDED (ApplyR3 (BrownGoose), converge r3 2026-10-04; absolute rows/hour floor replaced, converge r2 L2 and r3 L2-ResearchR3.jsonl:1; history only, not a requirement):
every live surface declares expected rows/hour and an error-rate ceiling | healthy surfaces stay on.

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
on a sustained anomaly writes that surface's off-switch file with the reason.
acceptance_criteria:
Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s work/fleet-idle-watch -p 'test_fleet_idle_watch.py'`. In tests, plant a silent surface and an error-rate spike; each must alert and put the correct surface into its OFF state with a reason within one check, while a healthy surface whose rows per eligible host event sit inside its 7-day CI stays on, and an idle fleet (zero host traffic for 3 h) trips no off-switch; all three are unittest cases in work/fleet-idle-watch/test_fleet_idle_watch.py. Plant a stale/invalid telemetry row and prove it cannot be treated as healthy.
Switch registry (converge r4): the watcher reads each surface's switch path, polarity (presence-OFF such as cascade-off, read-screen-off, fleet-router.off; presence-ON sentinel such as memory-cap3, memory-filter-enforce) and owner from work/blast-radius/surfaces.json (jev-w2mf), the same registry jev-mvvh, jev-z885 and the jev-b35c.19 installer manifest use; OFF is defined per entry. Planted test: a presence-ON surface is turned off by removing its file and a presence-OFF surface by creating its file; the wrong polarity fails the test. Surfaces with no switch file today (native find, auto-thinking, smart stop) are listed with off_switch null: the watcher alerts on them and never reports them as switched off until a switch exists.
Restore (converge r4): an off surface emits no rows, so it can never show healthy telemetry. Restore is a probe window: the operator starts the surface in log-only (shadow) mode for a stated window; only if its rows per eligible host event sit inside the 7-day CI does the switch flip back ON. Planted tests: an OFF surface with zero rows never auto-restores; a probe window inside the CI permits the restore; a probe window outside it keeps the surface OFF.
Rehearsal without side effects (converge r4): add a --dry-run flag to scripts/fleet-idle-watch.py that routes every ntm send (page(), :915-947) to an in-process recorder. Run `HOME=$TMPDIR/06wt-home python3 scripts/fleet-idle-watch.py --once --dry-run` against a scratch copy of ~/.local/state/jev with one shadow log stopped for 2 h, so live switches are never written: confirm the scratch off-switch and reason appear and assert zero sends to pane 1 (planted: a --dry-run run that calls ntm fails the test).
Supervised service (converge r4): the watcher runs under launchd (work/fleet-idle-watch/ai.jev.fleet-idle-watch.plist, KeepAlive) and writes a liveness row to ~/.local/state/jev/fleet-watch-liveness.jsonl every check; a killed watcher is restarted by launchd, and a liveness row older than two checks turns doctor RED and pages pane 1 (FOR jev-b35c.3). Planted: kill -9 the watcher, a new liveness row appears within two checks.
Then observe the actual watcher for one full hourly check: the silent surface and sustained-error surface are put in their OFF state, a healthy surface stays enabled, and the owner alert names the affected surface and reason. Verify the off-switch is scoped to that surface and the daily cap and fail-open behavior are unchanged. No claim of Jev quality or benefit.

Planted test: watcher auto-off during a scheduler ON window, then the scheduler runs, and the surface stays off. The live observation of 'the actual watcher' runs only after the fleet watcher is restarted (it is STOPPED, ROADMAP.md cadence), with the restart named as a step.

SUPERSEDED (ApplyR3 (BrownGoose), converge r3 2026-10-04; first paragraph restated per eligible host event; history only, not a requirement):

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s work/fleet-idle-watch -p 'test_fleet_idle_watch.py'`. In tests, plant a silent surface and an error-rate spike; each must alert and write the correct surface's off-switch with a reason within one check, while a healthy surface whose rows per eligible host event sit inside its 7-day CI stays on, and an idle fleet (zero host traffic for 3 h) trips no off-switch; all three are unittest cases in work/fleet-idle-watch/test_fleet_idle_watch.py. Plant a stale/invalid telemetry row and prove it cannot be treated as healthy. Then run `python3 scripts/fleet-idle-watch.py --once` against the live state (~/.local/state/jev/), with HOME pointed at a scratch state root (`HOME=$TMPDIR/06wt-home`, holding a copy of ~/.local/state/jev with one shadow log stopped for 2 h) so the live switches are never written; confirm the scratch off-switch file and reason appear; then observe the actual watcher for one full hourly check: the silent surface and sustained-error surface are disabled, a healthy surface stays enabled, and the owner alert names the affected surface and reason. Verify the off-switch is scoped to that surface, the daily cap and fail-open behavior are unchanged, and an operator can restore the switch only after healthy telemetry. title: Preflight: refuse a live run whose preregistered bar is unreachable (power/reachability check)
description: WHAT: A keyless checker, scripts/bar-reachable.py, that reads a prereg's arms from committed baseline/floor rows and computes the best achievable test result for the stated bar before any call. For paired McNemar: the maximum discordant pairs given the oracle headroom over the comparator on the exact prereg keys, and the smallest attainable p. For rate bars: the Wilson bound at a perfect score. Exit 1 when the bar cannot be met even by a perfect Jev arm; exit 0 with the numbers otherwise. WHY: jev-jjwt's prereg (c0ef4468) passed size and offered-answer feasibility, but its McNemar bar was unreachable (best single 22/24, max 2 discordant, p >= 0.5). Pane 1 caught it by hand; RULE 15 clause 4 names only size and offered-action checks. Emerald segment 2 (a523dc50) is the same class: its goal was solved by the prior. ACCEPTANCE: a unittest built on committed rows: jev-jjwt's 24-task split must exit 1 with max discordant 2; R112's 337-task two-archive split must exit 0 (b=2, c=8 showed room). A planted edit that drops the discordant computation must turn a test red. Registered in TESTS.md. Non-author check before close. No Jev call.
close_reason: VERDICT (non-author pane 1): HOLDS at ee16906d over 6e4ff307/d777d80b/c1cb58fe/33345879. python3 -m unittest scripts/test_bar_reachable.py -> 4 OK in a clean clone. The flip test uses committed floor rows (30 tasks, comparator 20 exact, oracle headroom 3): UNREACHABLE, exit 1, min p 0.25. Plant minimum_p = exact_mcnemar_p(tasks - comparator_exact, 0) at bar-reachable.py:178 -> that test FAILS; restored, cmp identical. jev-jjwt split still refused.

comments.author: AmberWillow
comments.text: NON-AUTHOR CHECK (pane 1) of 6e4ff307: tests OK in a clean clone; plant max_wins = tasks (drop comparator subtraction) -> 2 tests FAIL, restored byte-identical (cmp). One fail-open gap, not closed: mcnemar_reachability sets max_discordant_wins = tasks - comparator_exact (bar-reachable.py:147), which assumes Jev can complete every task the comparator misses. For a choice over fixed candidates (Best-of-N) the ceiling is the tasks where some offered candidate completes and the comparator does not (oracle headroom). Without it the gate says REACHABLE when no offered option can win. Fix: optional --oracle-exact (or per-task oracle rows) capping max wins at oracle_exact - both_exact, plus a test built from floor_receipt.json where the tasks minus comparator count exceeds the oracle headroom. Resume after the planning duel.

comments.author: AmberWillow
comments.text: NON-AUTHOR CHECK (pane 1) of d777d80b: not closed. Tests OK in a clean clone (3/3). Plant: reverted minimum_p to exact_mcnemar_p(tasks - comparator_exact, 0) (the old fail-open) -> unittest still OK, restored cmp identical. So no test pins the fix: no fixture has oracle headroom below the comparator's misses. Also score_receipt_headroom (bar-reachable.py:147) uses observed Jev-vs-best discordance b+c as 'headroom'; that is what one Jev run did, not the ceiling (tasks where some offered candidate completes and the comparator does not). Needed: derive headroom per task from floor_receipt.json results_by_task over the offered candidates, plus a test built from committed rows where headroom < misses and the gate must say UNREACHABLE while tasks - comparator_exact would say REACHABLE. Resume after the planning duel.

comments.text: NON-AUTHOR CHECK (pane 1) of c1cb58fe: closer, still not closed. unittest OK (3/3) in a clean clone. Plant: minimum_p = exact_mcnemar_p(tasks - comparator_exact, 0) at line 178 -> tests still OK (restored, cmp identical), because R112 is REACHABLE either way (74 and 198 both give p < 0.05). title: Numeric claim check by Choice over evidence numbers (masked value), code compare; last round
description:
WHAT: one round of a different primitive for numeric claim checking. For each number in a claim, mask it in its clause ("[N]") and ask a Jev Choice which of the narrowed evidence's own number tokens gives that quantity, or "not stated". Then code compares the chosen token with the claimed value (exact, or the evidence value rounded to the claim's precision). Same two corpora (19 README claims of jev-sp5, 34 close reasons of jev-10t) and the same narrowed evidence as jev-h8s. Fresh plants from a new seed: digit plants (one digit changed by a rule that differs from all earlier rounds), plus role plants (the claimed value replaced by another number token from the same evidence, the exact role-confusion case). A feasibility arm of unambiguous single-number sentences must pass. Bar committed before any call. Role plants are reported separately.
WHY: jev-h8s (R83 retry 2) failed, and 3 of its 4 false confirmations were role confusion: a value present in the evidence in another role. A Noul asked "is value X stated" finds X anywhere. A Choice over the evidence's numbers with the claimed value hidden has to identify the quantity. It is a different primitive, not a fourth Noul wording.

title: Arm sanity check: compare a live arm's action-type mix with its reference arm after the first rows, and stop degenerate arms early
description:
WHAT: scripts/arm-sanity.py --arm <decisions.jsonl> --reference <decisions.jsonl> [--min-rows 200]. Classifies each decision's chosen action into a type (PokéJev: switch / move / tera, from the chosen string; MiniWoB: the verb before '[' such as click / type / select / none) and, among decisions where more than one type was offered, prints the per-type choice rate for both files, the absolute difference, and a two-proportion z. Exit 1 when any type's rate differs by more than --max-diff (default 0.25) with |z| > 4, or when one type takes >= 0.95 of choices while the reference is <= 0.80; exit 0 otherwise; exit 2 NOT_RUN when either file has fewer than --min-rows eligible decisions. (1) CHRONOLOGY: for every result row in EVAL.md, every bead claiming a live quality number, and every committed bar file a live measurement reads (including work/jev-mvvh/harm-costs.json, the value ledger's harm costs, jev-mvvh AC3), every commit that touches the bar's threshold/estimand lines precedes the first call. Post-hoc bars fail. Timestamps: the receipt row's ts when present; otherwise the first commit time of the row file (`git log --diff-filter=A --format=%cI -- <rows>`); a bar kept in a bead comment is dated by the first commit of .beads/issues.jsonl that contains its text (`git log -S`), never by the editable comment created_at. For bars measured on organic hook logs (jev-mvvh, jev-9cqw, X8, jev-nwo1), where outcome rows exist before any bar, the bar commit is compared with the first commit or extract of the outcome rows, not with the first call.
(2) RECEIPT FIELDS: every result row names its incumbent arm and the sha256 of the shared row-id set both arms were scored on, plus N, date, model id and spend. A missing field is FAIL, not UNVERIFIABLE; an incumbent scored on a different row-id set is FAIL.
Missing bar hash: a row committed before this gate lands that has no bar sha256 is UNVERIFIABLE for chronology (never PASS); a row committed after it lands without ts or bar sha256 is FAIL. jev-oh7c's commit gate makes new result rows carry ts and the bar file's sha256.
WHY: ROADMAP.md pillar 3 (Honest) says no check enforces bar-before-call (MISSION-AUDIT.md section 2); AmberWillow converge r1 L1 found no bead owns it. Converge r4: bead-lint only lints bead structure, so a green Honest check said nothing about incumbents, N, model id or spend (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:64, fresh-conductor-c.jsonl:5); comment created_at is a mutable field in a git-tracked JSONL (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:55); the cited committed receipt rows carry neither ts nor bar hash, so real rows were almost all UNVERIFIABLE with no stated rule (fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:26). scripts/result_commit_evidence.py (jev-oh7c, untracked until oh7c commits it) already refuses result rows without rows/scorer; this extends that gate, so this bead depends on jev-oh7c.

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):

Title: Gate: every quality bar is committed before its first live call
acceptance_criteria:
creates: scripts/bar_chronology.py, scripts/test_bar_chronology.py.
1. `python3 -m unittest scripts/test_bar_chronology.py` passes.
2. Planted negatives (chronology): a fixture where the bar commit is 1 s after the first receipt row fails with the bar path, commit time and first-call time named; a bar committed 1 s before passes. A bar committed 1 day before the first call whose threshold is edited 1 s after it -> FAIL. A bead-comment bar whose comment created_at is backdated but whose first containing commit of .beads/issues.jsonl is after the first call -> FAIL. An organic-log bar committed after the outcome rows were first committed -> FAIL.
3. Planted negatives (receipt fields): a result row with no incumbent arm, no row-id-set hash, no N, no date, no model id or no spend FAILs naming the missing field; an incumbent scored on a different row-id set than the challenger FAILs; a complete row passes.
4. `python3 scripts/bar_chronology.py --since 2026-09-24 --json` runs over the real EVAL.md rows and the committed bar files live measurements read (work/jev-mvvh/harm-costs.json included) and lists every row as PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIABLE with the timestamp source used (ts, row-file first commit, or bead-comment first commit); UNVERIFIABLE is never counted as PASS. With `--strict` it exits non-zero on any FAIL and on any UNVERIFIABLE row committed after this gate's landing commit.
5. Rule (converge r2 L4, work/plan-20261004/convergence/r2/L4-HonestyR2.jsonl:11): every commit that touches the bar file's threshold/estimand lines (`git log --follow -p` on the bar file) must predate the first receipt; when a row carries the sha256 of the bar file, a mismatch with the file's content at first-call time FAILs; a row committed before this gate with no bar hash is UNVERIFIABLE.
6. .omp/mission.toml's honest pillar check runs `python3 scripts/bar_chronology.py --since 2026-09-24 --json --strict` together with bead-lint, and its beads list names jev-6gun.
7. Non-author re-runs 1-4; close with commit:<sha> on origin/main.

title: Validate agent-beacon's Jev promotion rubric on our own session ground truth
description: WHAT: Beacon (Asymptote-Labs/agent-beacon@c8d56ad, MIT) decides which agent sessions become reusable skills with three Jev Nouls (cli/beacon/internal/learning/evaluator.go:31-50: task success; reusable correction or debugging pattern; lesson supported by concrete events). title: Restart every jev pane onto current hooks; prove zero stale-hook rows
description:

Restart every jev worker pane not yet restarted (ntm respawn), then show 30 min of rows with zero permission-required / recipient-and-data-class reasons. ACCEPTANCE: count of stale-reason rows in the 30 min after restart = 0; scored rows present. NO-CLAIM: not benefit.
REALITY CHECK 2026-10-01: fleet sat idle ~6h because the ready queue was empty and every benefit question waited passively for traffic. Native Jev runs ~8,400 calls/day (find 7,137, auto-thinking 703, unexpected-stop 309, ttsr 285 in 24h) but no surface has a measured benefit. Rules: bar fixed in a bead comment BEFORE reading outcome data; live calls bounded, spend stated; non-author verifier closes; NO-CLAIM line.
WHY: panes kept running hooks loaded before their fix; gate-observe and injection-shadow logged stale reason codes (permission-required, recipient-and-data-class) after the code changed, so measured rates mixed old and new behaviour (ROADMAP.md pillar current).
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/jev-6pjh/stale_filter.jq, work/jev-6pjh/test_stale_filter.py.
The stale marker sits in different fields in the two logs (bead comments 1815 and 1818): gate-observe writes status NOT_RUN with error 'reason=permission-required', and injection-shadow writes .reason 'recipient-and-data-class-approval-required'. A filter over .reason alone counts 0 on gate-observe whatever code is loaded, so it cannot fail there (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:19,47, fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:5, fresh-conductor-b.jsonl:16). work/jev-6pjh/stale_filter.jq holds the one filter both checks use: rows with $start <= .ts < $end whose ((.reason // "") + " " + (.error // "") + " " + (.status // "")) matches permission-required|recipient-and-data-class, counted. Per file run `jq -s -f work/jev-6pjh/stale_filter.jq --arg start "$START" --arg end "$END" <file>` on ~/.local/state/jev/gate-observe.jsonl and ~/.local/state/jev/injection-shadow.jsonl.
1. `python3 -m unittest work/jev-6pjh/test_stale_filter.py -v` runs stale_filter.jq over planted rows in each log shape: a gate-observe row with the marker only in .error (status NOT_RUN) and an injection-shadow row with the marker only in .reason must both count; a scored row with no marker must not. Planted negative: a .reason-only filter fails this test.
2. POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST, per file: the same command over the fixed historical window START=2026-10-02T16:44:40Z, END=2026-10-03T16:44:40Z must print a nonzero count (613 gate-observe and 724 injection-shadow per comment 1818); record the sha256 of that window's extracted rows in the evidence comment so a re-check reads the same rows. A zero control makes the check invalid, never a pass.
3. For each pane restarted in a safe window, the 30 minutes after restart give 0 stale rows per file, with at least one status == "scored" row in each window.
4. The evidence comment gives pane IDs, restart times, time windows, counts and each pane's loaded hook identity (see Historical cause). Do not force-restart a pane with active work; pane 1 remains unverified until safely restarted. NO-CLAIM: this proves hook freshness only, not benefit. SOURCE: bead jev-6pjh comments 1694, 1815 and 1818; fix commit df2cf0d9. Cite this bead by id: .beads/issues.jsonl:98 is jev-6ngv, not this bead (fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:81).

comments.text:
WHAT
Separate the EXPECTATION from the RECEIPT in docs/demos/STATUS.tsv so a row's number cannot be
validated against a file the row's own author wrote. Today scripts/lane-status.sh verifies that a
cited receipt EXISTS on disk (fail-closed, exit 3, RED arm proven with a planted bogus row). It does
not verify that the receipt's VALUE agrees with a separately-recorded expectation. Existence is not
agreement.

WHY
This is the lane's most-measured defect class, not a speculative one.
  * Three candidates were scored both ways and all three fell the same direction — authored
    success, real-data miss: a gate at 0/20 FP authored vs 3/20 held-out; foreman supervision
    AUC 1.000 on vignettes vs 0.750 on 186,449 real windows; jev-review 12/12 authored pairs vs
    AUC 0.625 on 22 real diffs (RULING-authored-vs-real-20260919.md).
  * R70: "our kills are auditable, our ships are not" — FP samples were never persisted, so a
    number existed that nobody but its author could check.
  * 2026-09-21: a 219-row corpus was reported with aggregates only and no pair identities. Caught
    by a peer, not by a gate. A validator that checks existence would have passed it.
  * Same day, dumpTools was cited as an L2 oracle by two panes; it is blind to extension tools. A
    value check against an independent expectation would have caught the false ZERO; an existence
    check would not.

ACCEPTANCE
  Command: ./scripts/lane-status.sh   (plus its selftest)
  POSITIVE: every STATUS.tsv row carries an expectation field recorded independently of the
    receipt, and lane-status.sh exits 0 only when receipt value == expectation for every row.
  PLANTED NEGATIVE (required, must be shown failing): a row whose receipt EXISTS but whose value
    DISAGREES with its expectation must exit non-zero. The current validator passes that case —
    demonstrate the current pass, then the new fail. Without both halves this is unproven.
  NO-CLAIM: this gates arithmetic agreement only. It does not detect a wrong expectation, a
    corpus the author also chose, or a metric that is the wrong metric.

CREATION GATE (tick.md section 1 — all four named)
  1. CONSUMER: scripts/lane-status.sh, and every pane that cites a STATUS verdict.
  2. GATE: a verdict cannot ship when its receipt disagrees with its expectation.
  3. OBSERVED DEFECT: the four instances above, all measured in this repo, none speculative.
  4. RETIREMENT: retire when every STATUS row's number is derived from a receipt produced by
     someone other than the row's author, making the agreement check redundant.

title: Ship recover: wire the bake-off winner into its host tool, L3 both ways, value receipt, KEEP/KILL
description:
WHAT: the ship step for the `recover` decision family (retry, change or re-read after an error; work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:223). Once its bake-off (jev-n4-recover-error-rule-1grh) commits a RECEIPT naming a winning arm, wire that arm, through its cohort A adapter (jev-b35c.16) and behind its decision contract kit/contracts/recover.json, into its host tool: the next call after a bash/edit error, through a post-tool hook (no incumbent today). Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. When the receipt names no winner (REFUTED, DROPPED-UNLABELLED, or no arm beat the incumbent) nothing is wired: the bead records NOT-SHIPPED with that receipt and closes. A rule arm that wins ships the same way with zero model calls. Labels: 6,644 organic next-call outcomes.
WHY: converge r4 (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:87, fresh-conductor-c.jsonl:1) found no bead that takes a winning family arm into a host tool and produces its L3 and value receipts, so stage 1 (jev-uzq1) could close with every family CODE, REFUTED or DROPPED and none in a tool, against the mission's 'proven live' (ROADMAP.md mission line and 'Done for a feature'). Joshua decision 2 (converge r4): one P0 ship-winner bead per family that has or will have labels, which jev-uzq1 depends on.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/ship/recover/SHIP.md, kit/test/ship-recover.test.mjs.
1. `node --test kit/test/ship-recover.test.mjs` passes keylessly with injected backends against the copy the host loads: the wired arm acts on a committed real positive fixture and stays quiet on a planted negative; with the off switch set it makes zero classifier calls and the host turn proceeds; with the backend down, slow or capped it takes the contract's safe side within the latency budget. Planted negatives: a wiring that ignores the off switch fails; a host file that imports or calls askJev directly instead of going through the seam fails; a wiring attempted with no RECEIPT naming a winning arm is refused. (UPHILL: the test pins the contract the omp-kit change must meet.)
2. Both ways L3: after the expected.json row is added, jev-grzn's harness (work/l3-receipts/run.py, created by jev-grzn) writes a positive and a planted-negative receipt for this surface with session file path, log row, answering model id and spend; a FAIL turns the surface OFF, never left ON.
3. Value: jev-mvvh's ledger prints a row for this surface with verdict KEEP, PROMOTE or KILL and its reason; the value receipt is a KEEP or PROMOTE row; on KILL the off switch is flipped and a fresh session writes zero rows for the surface.
4. work/ship/recover/SHIP.md records the bake-off RECEIPT path and winning arm, the host path and off switch, the L3 receipt rows, the ledger row and the KEEP/PROMOTE/KILL verdict; or NOT-SHIPPED with the receipt that refuted, dropped or found no winner; or UPHILL with the omp-kit bead id. jev-uzq1 reads this file for the family's verdict.
5. A non-author re-runs 1-3; close with commit:<sha>.

description:
WHAT: the ship step for the `gate` decision family (command risky (observe layer); work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:230). Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. When the receipt names no winner (REFUTED, DROPPED-UNLABELLED, or no arm beat the incumbent) nothing is wired: the bead records NOT-SHIPPED with that receipt and closes. A rule arm that wins ships the same way with zero model calls. Labels: blind 396 rows with 47 harm; Joshua decision 4 restates X7's 47/47 as a recall lower bound of about 0.68 from a sample stratified on Jev's own flag, so an unflagged-stratum sample is required before Jev is wired as the gate winner.

title: Loss depth: AX pruning (R107): why Jev kept the whole page on 20/50 episodes, and whether pruning can ever pay with a Jev planner
description: WHAT: keyless autopsy of the 100 jev-arm pruner requests in work/miniwob-ax-prune/rows/{dev,heldout}-jev.jsonl (per-node Noul answers). (3) Ranked one-variable hypotheses for a dev loop: one Noul instead of three OR'd; a keep cut fitted on dev; a cheaper pruner state (node text only). title: Memory filter: bundle all memory judgments of a turn into one Jev request

import csv, re, sys
claims_p, ledger_p, out_p, needle = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
lines = open(ledger_p).read().split('\n')
hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if needle in l]
assert len(hits) == 1, "needle must occur exactly once"
i = hits[0]
sents = re.split(r"(?<=[.!])\s+|\s*\|\s*", lines[i])
tgt = [s for s in sents if needle in s]
assert len(tgt) == 1, "needle must hit exactly one sentence"
pats = []
with open(claims_p) as fh:
    for row in csv.DictReader(fh, delimiter="\t"):
        p = row.get("readme_pattern") or ""
        if p and p.lower() in tgt[0].lower():
            pats.append(p)
assert pats, "no registered pattern in needle sentence"
new_line = lines[i]
for p in pats:
    new_line = re.sub(re.escape(p), "", new_line, flags=re.I)
assert len(new_line) >= 20 and re.search(r"\d", new_line), "remnant must stay a candidate"
lines[i] = new_line
open(out_p, "w").write("\n".join(lines))

title: Ship reread: wire the bake-off winner into its host tool, L3 both ways, value receipt, KEEP/KILL
description:
WHAT: the ship step for the `reread` decision family (skip a repeat read; work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:220). Once its bake-off (jev-n2-reread-dedup-rule-i817) commits a RECEIPT naming a winning arm, wire that arm, through its cohort A adapter (jev-b35c.16) and behind its decision contract kit/contracts/reread.json, into its host tool: repeat-read handling: today's read-dedup shadow; the winner is N2's content-hash + line-range rule unless a model arm beats it. Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. When the receipt names no winner (REFUTED, DROPPED-UNLABELLED, or no arm beat the incumbent) nothing is wired: the bead records NOT-SHIPPED with that receipt and closes. A rule arm that wins ships the same way with zero model calls. Labels: 20,388 redundant reads (a tautological label; N2 builds the residual-harm label).
WHY: converge r4 (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:87, fresh-conductor-c.jsonl:1) found no bead that takes a winning family arm into a host tool and produces its L3 and value receipts, so stage 1 (jev-uzq1) could close with every family CODE, REFUTED or DROPPED and none in a tool, against the mission's 'proven live' (ROADMAP.md mission line and 'Done for a feature'). Joshua decision 2 (converge r4): one P0 ship-winner bead per family that has or will have labels, which jev-uzq1 depends on.

creates: work/ship/reread/SHIP.md, kit/test/ship-reread.test.mjs.
1. `node --test kit/test/ship-reread.test.mjs` passes keylessly with injected backends against the copy the host loads: the wired arm acts on a committed real positive fixture and stays quiet on a planted negative; with the off switch set it makes zero classifier calls and the host turn proceeds; with the backend down, slow or capped it takes the contract's safe side within the latency budget. Planted negatives: a wiring that ignores the off switch fails; a host file that imports or calls askJev directly instead of going through the seam fails; a wiring attempted with no RECEIPT naming a winning arm is refused. (UPHILL: the test pins the contract the omp-kit change must meet.)
2. Both ways L3: after the expected.json row is added, jev-grzn's harness (work/l3-receipts/run.py, created by jev-grzn) writes a positive and a planted-negative receipt for this surface with session file path, log row, answering model id and spend; a FAIL turns the surface OFF, never left ON.
3. Value: jev-mvvh's ledger prints a row for this surface with verdict KEEP, PROMOTE or KILL and its reason; the value receipt is a KEEP or PROMOTE row; on KILL the off switch is flipped and a fresh session writes zero rows for the surface.
4. work/ship/reread/SHIP.md records the bake-off RECEIPT path and winning arm, the host path and off switch, the L3 receipt rows, the ledger row and the KEEP/PROMOTE/KILL verdict; or NOT-SHIPPED with the receipt that refuted, dropped or found no winner; or UPHILL with the omp-kit bead id. jev-uzq1 reads this file for the family's verdict.
5. A non-author re-runs 1-3; close with commit:<sha>.

WHAT: one CLI, binary `classifier` with alias `clf`, that applies typed classifiers (Choice/Score/Noul, calibrated, abstain path) to the work this fleet touches, with the backend a flag (--backend jev|clef|auto). Sixteen decision families (work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md section 8), a doctor that tells the truth, a `ready` audit for new projects, an installer with uninstall/rollback. WHY: three weeks of research produced measured surfaces and refuted designs but no product; Joshua 2026-10-04: 'turn it into actual product families within a single cli'. Name decision: Joshua 2026-10-04 'its own path - classifier or something that properly names it not to a sspecific model'. SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md (commit f27effcc + row 7/9 fix); specs in work/plan-20261004/specs/. Accounting node only; never dispatched. It has NO blocking edges to its own children (converge r4, L5-GraphR4.jsonl:1): br and bv treat parent-child as blocking, so an epic->child blocks edge forms a cycle with each child's parent-child edge and deadlocked 34 of 88 plan beads (the epic, all 28 children, jev-1yqu, jev-grzn, jev-r1vp, jev-uzq1 and the root). The children hang off it by parent-child only; jev-q3q8 blocks on every non-dropped child directly; the epic closes through `br epic close-eligible` once every child is closed. It is not deferred either, since a deferred parent blocks its children.

SUPERSEDED (ApplyR3 (BrownGoose), converge r3 2026-10-04; family count, L2-ResearchR3.jsonl:11; history only, not a requirement):
Ten families ranked by evidence

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
It blocks on every non-closed child (converge r3 L5-GraphR3.jsonl:11), so `br ready` cannot offer it before they close.
acceptance_criteria:
Every child bead of jev-b35c closed by non-author verification; `classifier overview --json` on a fresh install lists every family with its backend, bar, and last eval result.

CLOSURE SCOPE (credit-GoldRiver.jsonl:15): every dotted child jev-b35c.N counts, including the measurement, installer, family-cohort, chain and overview children added in wave 1; `RUST_LOG=off br list --all --json | jq '[.issues[]|select((.id|startswith("jev-b35c.")) and .status != "closed")]|length'` must be 0 before the epic closes: open, in_progress and in_review children all count (converge r4, fresh-conductor-e.jsonl:11; the old query counted only `--status open`). Dropped and folded children (.8, .11, .12, .13, .26, .27) close on a committed investigation artifact (work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md for the family drops) by a non-author. Planted negative: a jev-b35c -> jev-b35c.N blocks edge fails bead-lint (an epic blocking on its own child is a readiness cycle).

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
`RUST_LOG=off br list --status open --json | jq '[.issues[]|select(.id|startswith("jev-b35c."))]|length'` must be 0 before the epic closes.

title: classifier CLI: rename + shell (bin, argv did-you-mean, help/version exit 0, exit codes, envelope)
description:
WHAT: add bins `classifier` and `clf` to kit (package name: `jev-kit` stays the unpublished package name in stage 1; nothing is published to npm, where `classifier` is taken, and jev-r1vp installs from a fresh clone; recorded in work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md section 1), argv parser with Levenshtein did-you-mean, bare/--help/--version exit 0, one exit-code module (0,1,3,4,5,6,64,66,73,74; 3 = refused, e.g. an unoffered label; no key = 1; the same dictionary as PRODUCT.md:18), one JSON envelope classifier.<cmd>.v1 {ok,schema,status,data,meta,warnings,commands,errors}. Every existing kit/bin/jev.mjs verb is reachable as `classifier <verb>`; the `jev` bin is removed from kit/package.json because the mission rejects the `jev` binary name (.omp/mission.toml:16, hermes-jev-skills keeps it), and `jev-skill-gap` stays only as a deprecation shim. WHY: today --help/--version exit 1, unknown flags like --robto are silently ignored, decision verbs exit 1 on no key while README says 2 (specs/cli-ergonomics-spec.md section 0). Tasks ergo T1-T4. SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md (commit f27effcc + row 7/9 fix); specs in work/plan-20261004/specs/ CONTRACT (every implementation bead in this epic): (1) the failing test is committed or shown failing in a bead comment (command + output) before the change; (2) one planted mutation of the change that the test catches, with the command; (3) any regex that runs on tool output, model text or commands passes the regex-engineering skill section 7 run (match / no-match / near-miss on a 50k-char adversarial input < 50 ms); (4) any Jev/Clef quality claim has its bar committed before the first call and states spend; (5) a non-author verifies in a clone with a scrubbed HOME before close. No live calls unless the bead says so.

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
add bins `classifier` and `clf` to kit (package name TBD: `classifier` is taken on npm)
Existing jev.mjs verbs keep working through the new shell.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: kit/test/cli-argv.test.mjs, kit/test/cli-envelope.test.mjs, kit/test/cli-exit.test.mjs, kit/test/cli-help.test.mjs, kit/test/cli-bins.test.mjs.
One binding list (converge r4: the STRUCTURE, CLI CONTRACT, HONEST-CREDIT and RESOLVED layers below are folded into it; the old layers are kept verbatim under SUPERSEDED as history, not as requirements). Close command: `node --test kit/test/cli-argv.test.mjs kit/test/cli-help.test.mjs kit/test/cli-exit.test.mjs kit/test/cli-envelope.test.mjs kit/test/cli-bins.test.mjs` and `npm test --prefix kit` both pass.
1. Failing-first: each of the five tests is committed (or shown failing in a bead comment with command and output) before the change, and exercises the production entrypoints and the shared parser/exit/envelope modules.
2. Bins: kit/package.json `bin` keys are exactly `classifier`, `clf` and the `jev-skill-gap` deprecation shim; `classifier` and `clf` run the same CLI. Planted negative: a `jev` bin key in kit/package.json fails kit/test/cli-bins.test.mjs (mission rejection, .omp/mission.toml:16).
3. Help: bare `classifier`, `--help`, `-h`, `help` and `--version` exit 0; deleting a help footer fails the golden help test.
4. Argv: `classifier --robto` exits 64 with a did-you-mean and the exact corrected command on stderr; a distant unknown flag (`--zzzz`) exits 64 with no suggestion; `--apply` and other destructive flags are never auto-corrected. Planted negative: an unknown flag that exits 0 fails the test.
5. Exit codes: one module with the PRODUCT.md section 1 dictionary (0,1,3,4,5,6,64,66,73,74). A keyless decision verb exits 1 with status NOT_RUN (decision D1; this supersedes exit 2 in specs/cli-ergonomics-spec.md section 2.4/E5/T3, so no open no-key conflict remains); `--fake` returns a valid result; an unoffered label or malformed answer exits 3 with status REFUSED, never NOT_RUN; the output mode never changes the exit status.
6. Envelope: `classifier.<cmd>.v1 {ok,schema,status,data,meta,warnings,commands,errors}` parses; JSON goes to stdout and diagnostics to stderr; output is byte-deterministic under `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` after removing only `meta.latency_ms` and `meta.usage`. Planted negative: `latency_ms` inside `data` fails the determinism test; removing a required envelope field fails the schema test. `NO_COLOR=1` leaks no colour; piped/non-TTY and `CI=true` runs never prompt; golden help and schema tests run in CI.
7. Legacy verbs: every verb kit/bin/jev.mjs dispatches today runs as `classifier <verb>`; README and stranger-run rows that call `jev` are moved to `classifier` in the same change.
8. A non-author verifies in a clone with a scrubbed HOME before close. NO-CLAIM: keyless/fake tests prove the CLI contract only, not model quality or live behaviour.

Assert `--zzzz` gets no suggestion and `--apply` is never auto-corrected; help/version exits 0 and deleting a help footer makes the test fail; `--fake` succeeds while an unoffered label exits 3 rather than NOT_RUN; and envelopes parse and remain byte-deterministic after removing only `meta.latency_ms` and `meta.usage`. Plant `latency_ms` inside `data` and assert the determinism test fails. SOURCE: `work/plan-20261004/specs/cli-ergonomics-spec.md:280-285`.

CLI CONTRACT (cli-CyanPeak.jsonl:1): Failing-first tests: `classifier --robto` exits 64 with a did-you-mean on stderr; `classifier --help` exits 0; `classifier classify --fake --robot` emits a valid envelope; keyless decision verb exits 1 with status NOT_RUN. Planted negative: an unknown flag never exits 0. `npm test --prefix kit` green. Also pin `classifier`, `clf`, and every global invocation: `--json`/`--robot` envelope schema, shared exit code/status dictionary, typo correction and exact corrective command on stderr; deterministic JSON under `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` (same bytes except documented volatile fields); `NO_COLOR=1` and non-TTY/CI behavior; golden help and schema tests run in CI. Acceptance test fails if an unknown flag is ignored, output mode changes exit status, an unrecognized flag lacks the exact suggested correction, color leaks under `NO_COLOR`, or output is nondeterministic. Sources: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:18-20,43-44; work/plan-20261004/specs/cli-ergonomics-spec.md:180-226; ~/.agents/skills/agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools/references/rubric/SCORING-RUBRIC.md:70-78,86-110,136-144,168-194; ~/.agents/skills/agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools/references/methodology/JSON-SCHEMA-PATTERNS.md:7-23.

HONEST-CREDIT (credit-GoldRiver.jsonl:1): Failing-first keyless tests exercise the production CLI entrypoints and shared parser/exit/envelope modules. `classifier` and `clf` invoke the same CLI; bare, `--help`, `-h`, `help`, and `--version` exit 0; the recorded `--robto` typo is tested against the documented safe suggestion, distant unknown flags exit 64 without a suggestion, and destructive flags are never auto-corrected. Decision verbs without a key return NOT_RUN with the selected exit code; `--fake` returns a valid result; malformed/unoffered answers return REFUSED. Verify exact envelope fields, JSON stdout/stderr separation, documented deterministic fields, and legacy `jev` invocations/stranger-run rows. Resolve the documented no-key exit conflict before implementation and sync all docs/tests to the selected code. Planted negatives: unknown flag succeeds; required envelope field removed; destructive flag auto-corrected; each must fail its named test. Run `npm run prepare --prefix kit && node --test kit/test/*.test.mjs`; retain failing-first evidence and non-author scrubbed-HOME verification. NO-CLAIM: keyless/fake tests prove CLI contract only, not model quality or live behavior.

RESOLVED (conductor, decision D1): a missing key exits 1 with status NOT_RUN, per PRODUCT.md section 1; this supersedes the exit 2 in specs/cli-ergonomics-spec.md section 2.4/E5/T3.

title: classifier measurement core: symmetric calibration, rerun spread, cost/NP cuts, prevalence formula, conformal sets (library only)
description:
WHAT: Library-only integration core for the stage-1 measurement-method beads: one zero-dependency TypeScript module exposing symmetric calibration and same-model rerun spread (jev-b35c.23: D2, D7), expected-cost and Neyman-Pearson cuts with the fixed-prevalence PPV formula (jev-b35c.24: D3, D4 formula, D16 NP bound) and split-conformal LAC sets (jev-b35c.25: D5). No CLI verb lives here: `calibrate`, `eval` and `watch` and their envelope/exit/golden pins belong to jev-b35c.5 and the family beads jev-b35c.16/.17, which depend on this bead. Not in stage 1 (converge r4): BBSE, the KS alarm, BH/e-BH, confidence sequences and PPI++ (no consumer; D4 reversed by its own replay). Never turn missing labels, missing prerequisites, or unsupported assumptions into PASS.
WHY: the audit overturned three claims (Clef calibration win, Clef vendored win, memory .985) and explained the vendor .21 precision and the 0.990->0.335 skill-veto drop as method errors; each surviving method has a named consumer (calibration and rerun spread: every family eval; cuts: X7, X8; conformal: route --set).
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md section 7 D2, D3, D4, D5, D7, D16; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md sections A and B.
EVIDENCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md section 7; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
WHAT: Integration core for the D2-D7/D17 measurement-method beads: expose a zero-dependency TypeScript API for symmetric calibration, cost/prevalence/NP cuts, conformal abstention, multiplicity correction, same-model rerun spread, and prediction-powered metrics. Keep method work in independently verifiable child beads; never turn missing labels, missing prerequisites, or unsupported assumptions into PASS. WHY: the current core bundles seven distinct statistical decisions with separate assumptions and failure modes. SOURCE: `work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:166-172`; `work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:19-61`.
EVIDENCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:166-172; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:19-61

PRIOR DESCRIPTION (kept verbatim; scope now split as stated above):
WHAT: a zero-dependency TS module used by calibrate/eval/watch/ready: (1) probability floor 0.005 before fitting; temperature, Platt and isotonic (PAV) fitted on dev for every backend the same way; ECE with its noise floor and a seeded bootstrap CI; paired tests (McNemar, DeLong). (2) cuts by expected cost at projected prevalence; Neyman-Pearson cut from negatives only (29/59/149/299 negatives for FPR .10/.05/.02/.01, delta .05). (3) BBSE prevalence projection plus a KS alarm on live scores. (4) split-conformal LAC answer sets that refuse without an exchangeability declaration. (5) Benjamini-Hochberg across bars, e-BH within a batch, confidence sequences for shadow stopping. (6) prediction-powered inference for organic metrics. (7) drift tests against same-model rerun spread. WHY: the audit overturned three claims (Clef calibration win, Clef vendored win, memory .985) and explained the vendor .21 precision and the 0.990->0.335 skill-veto drop as method errors (D2-D7, D17). BORROW: port the design of franken_nlp src/calibration.rs (Dicklesworthstone mirror) and process_triage expected-loss/e-BH; no imports. SOURCE: Decision register: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md section 7; specs/advanced-mathops.md, advanced-literature.md, advanced-repos.md. CONTRACT: failing test committed (or shown failing) before the change; one planted mutation the test catches; any regex on tool/model text passes the regex-engineering section 7 run; any quality claim has its bar committed before the first call with spend stated; non-author verify in a clone with a scrubbed HOME. Keyless proofs run on committed rows only.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: kit/test/measurement.test.mjs.
STRUCTURE: `node --test kit/test/measurement.test.mjs` passes on committed, hash-identified rows and deterministic fake data. The integration test verifies the stage-1 method outputs are wired through the one module (calibration and rerun spread from .23, cuts and PPV formula from .24, conformal sets from .25) and that each child test file is present; it checks that no module imports a heavy runtime dependency and that missing/unsupported evidence reports NOT_RUN/UNKNOWN. Keyless reproductions on committed rows, with the tolerances fixed in the child beads: Jev Banking77 ECE after symmetric Platt ~.028 (Clef ~.025) with a paired CI that includes 0; LAC at alpha .10 coverage inside .25's Beta-Binomial interval; vendor Youden cut predicted precision ~.21 at 5% prevalence; the PPV formula at a GIVEN prevalence .29 reproduces .629/.399 from the D9 rates; NP cut within its FPR bound on an independent audit set; two same-model runs flagged only beyond the rerun envelope.
Planted negatives: a coin-flip calibration fixture and a non-exchangeable conformal fixture must make the relevant child test RED; a module that exports a CLI verb or reads argv fails the library-only test. Do not claim organic PPI, live calibration, or a metric win from synthetic fixtures. NO-CLAIM: reproduced committed rows validate this implementation only, not organic accuracy, transfer, or Clef advantage. SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md section 7; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md.

acceptance_criteria:
creates: kit/test/measurement-conformal.test.mjs.
`node --test kit/test/measurement-conformal.test.mjs` passes on committed calibration rows and deterministic generated fixtures. Parameters fixed here, before implementation (MATH REVIEW D5 below):
- Fixture: Jev Banking77 probabilities, work/choice-banking77/rows-full-jev.jsonl; calibration = the 200 DEV ids, test = the 600 held SAMPLE ids (seeds 8 and 7, work/local-decision-arms/run.py:24-26); n_cal = 200, n_test = 600; the sampling frame is named in the fixture header.
- alpha = .10. Score = 1 - p(true label) after the D2 probability floor of 0.005; q-hat = the ceil((n_cal+1)(1-alpha))-th smallest calibration score; a label is in the set iff its score <= q-hat (ties at q-hat are included); class ids carry no order.
- Coverage tolerance: with l = floor((n_cal+1)*alpha), held coverage must lie inside the central 95% interval of Beta-Binomial(n_test, n_cal+1-l, l), which the test computes exactly from n_cal, n_test and alpha; outside it reports FAIL. Mean set size and singleton share are reported, not gated.
- Metamorphic checks: permuting row order leaves sets and coverage unchanged (ID-keyed randomness); relabelling class ids permutes sets and leaves coverage and set size unchanged; an invalid probability vector (negative, NaN, or total mass outside 1 +/- 1e-6 before flooring) is refused with a typed reason.
Planted negatives: a non-exchangeable split (calibration and test drawn from different label distributions, or overlapping ids) and a caller that only declares exchangeability without a named sampling frame and disjoint calibration/test groups must REFUSE with a typed reason, never return sets; a coin-flip probability vector must produce near-full sets, never PASS on set size. Organic transfer stays NOT_RUN without eligible labels. SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md section 7 D5; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md T7.

MATH REVIEW (wave1, WildCarp; binding) for D5, kept verbatim:
- [plan:D5] LAC’s split-conformal formula is appropriate under exchangeability, but ‘refuse when exchangeability is not declared’ is too weak: a caller declaration does not establish exchangeability. Require a named sampling frame and disjoint calibration/test groups from the target population; otherwise abstain/refuse. Acceptance must state α, n_cal, n_test, tie handling, and a numeric finite-sample coverage interval or exact binomial criterion; ‘outside its finite-sample band’ is not executable. The reported .903 coverage / mean set 1.67 is an observed point, not a numerical tolerance. Add metamorphic checks: row permutation leaves the result unchanged with ID-keyed randomness; relabeling class IDs permutes sets but leaves coverage/set-size unchanged; strictly increasing score transforms preserve AUC (strictness matters with ties); invalid probability vectors refuse. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:170; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:33,54,118; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:115-117)

(evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:170; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:33,54,118; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:115-117)
- [plan:D6] The D6 accounting rule needs a defined family and valid input type: BH at q=.05 controls FDR only under independence or PRDS of valid p-values; e-BH requires valid e-values and its own batch/family boundaries. ‘Across the ledger’ and ‘within a batch’ are not enough to determine which hypotheses enter, how dependent/repeated bars are handled, or when recomputation occurs. Confidence sequences additionally require bounded outcomes and a declared dependence/cluster treatment and stopping rule. Add planted p/e-value inputs whose dependence violates the assumed regime; ensure invalid or missing p/e values cannot be silently dropped. The missing reversal criterion (‘—’) prevents an outcome-based refutation. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:171; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:35,60-61; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:158-160)
- [plan:D17] PPI is appropriate only with a probability sample of labels from the target population and predictions for that same population; the residual correction is not protected against convenience/active sampling unless the design weights are included. The bead’s reversal ‘PPI interval no narrower than labels-only’ needs equal nominal coverage and a specified estimator (PPI vs PPI++), random-label sampling, interval procedure, and numerical width comparison on repeated resamples. ‘PPI’ alone does not guarantee a narrower interval; PPI++/optimized rectifier is the method with a no-wider-than-classical property under its assumptions. Add metamorphic checks: when predictions are constant, PPI reduces to labels-only mean; when predictions equal labels on labeled rows, the residual correction is zero; permuting row order leaves estimates/CI unchanged with deterministic ID-keyed bootstrap. (evidence: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:182; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-literature.md:57,146-147; arXiv:2301.09633)

RESEARCH CORRECTION (converge r1 L2, research-misapplied, P2): D17's rationale ('organic positives are too sparse for labels-only estimates', citing m94x/9kmq) is not what PPI addresses. PPI (arXiv:2301.09633) gives valid CIs from a random labelled sample plus predictions, and narrows them only as predictions get more accurate. It does not create positives: on surfaces killed for ~0 organic positives (exposure gate), there is nothing to rectify for precision among flags. The reversal 'PPI interval no narrower than labels-only' is not guaranteed for plain PPI. PPI++ (arXiv:2311.01453) is the variant that 'always improve[s] on classical intervals'. D5 (LAC .903/1.67, R2) and D6 are supported, given e-BH controls FDR under any dependence (arXiv:2009.02824) and BH needs PRDS. FIX: Name PPI++ as the D17 estimator. Restate D17's WHY as 'cheaper CIs for prevalence/accuracy on surfaces WITH organic exposure'. Add a refusal when the labelled random sample contains fewer than k positives for a precision target, and keep exposure-zero surfaces on the `ready` row-2 FAIL path rather than PPI. title: classifier ready: the 18-row readiness audit for a new project
description:
WHAT: Implement `classifier ready <project-dir> --decision <spec>` as a pre-build audit for all 18 readiness rows. Emit PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN plus a checkable evidence path per row; any FAIL stops the build, and unavailable evidence is UNKNOWN rather than an inferred pass. Reuse the named exposure-check, bar-reachable, prevalence-check, audit_bars, row-provenance, wire-conformance, drift, and model-canary tools. WHY: prevent an ineligible or near-zero-positive classifier from reaching build/ship. SOURCE: `work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:69-95`; `work/plan-20261004/specs/classifier-areas.md:112-135,160-170`.
EVIDENCE: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:69-95; work/plan-20261004/specs/classifier-areas.md:112-135,160-170
acceptance_criteria:
creates: kit/test/ready.test.mjs.
STRUCTURE (beads-AmberWillow.jsonl:13): `node --test kit/test/ready.test.mjs` passes on committed fixtures. It exercises all 18 rows independently and asserts each emits PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN with a source path; the positive control in POSITIVE CONTROL below reaches the expected statuses, and a Banking77 route fixture must FAIL row 2 (exposure on real traffic) while passing rows 4 and 12, while planted zero-positive, unsupported-calibration, evidence-absent-from-judged-text, outcome-selected split, missing-key, and coin-flip-judge fixtures fail their corresponding rows and make the overall command RED. A missing evidence source yields UNKNOWN, never PASS. No live or deployment quality claim is made from fixtures. SOURCE: `work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:69-95`; `work/plan-20261004/specs/classifier-areas.md:112-135`.

CLI CONTRACT (cli-CyanPeak.jsonl:7): Replaying three of our own refuted designs through `ready` fails each at the row that killed it (m94x: positives; 9kmq: calibration support; compaction: recognition-vs-forecast or keep precision); the POSITIVE CONTROL below passes; Banking77 route is a negative replay that must FAIL row 2 (exposure) while passing rows 4 and 12 (converge r3 L2-ResearchR3.jsonl:37: Banking77 intent routing has no named decision or traffic in this fleet). Each row cites its source. `node --test kit/test/ready.test.mjs`. Pin `classifier ready --json`/`--robot` envelopes and status/exit mapping, unknown-flag exit 64 with did-you-mean and exact correction, error remediation command, deterministic row ordering and bytes under `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, `NO_COLOR=1`, and non-TTY/CI behavior; add a golden/schema pin in CI. Planted negative: input with a missing required source or a refuted design must not return PASS, and schema mutation must fail the pin. Sources: work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:27,43-44,69-95; ~/.agents/skills/agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools/references/rubric/SCORING-RUBRIC.md:70-78,86-110,136-144,168-194; ~/.agents/skills/agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools/references/rubric/REGRESSION-TEST-PATTERNS.md:1-23,40-58.

HONEST-CREDIT (credit-GoldRiver.jsonl:7): For `classifier ready <dir> --decision <spec>`, failing-first production-path tests assert exactly the 18 PRODUCT §4 rows are emitted, each with PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN and evidence path; any FAIL blocks the build and UNKNOWN is never PASS. The cited m94x, 9kmq, and compaction refutations fail the expected applicable rows; the POSITIVE CONTROL below passes; the Banking77 route case fails row 2 (exposure) and passes rows 4 and 12. A planted mutation that forces a refuted row to PASS must make the suite RED. Run `npm test --prefix kit`; report the named test and non-author scrubbed-HOME verification. No live calls. NO-CLAIM: these committed examples prove readiness logic only; they do not establish new-project quality or generalize to other corpora.

title: N3a route family: locate episodes + labels
description:
WHAT: define the locate episode (first locate call -> first read/edit of the file finally edited; one located file per episode, so tokens per episode = tokens per located file), capture episodes with N0's miner, and commit the PREREG, dev/held split and labels that X6 (jev-x6-intent-encoder-0u9a) and the N3b bake-off (jev-n3-route-locate-bakeoff-4xnz) both consume. Labels are mechanical (the locating tool, i.e. the tool whose result first contained the path finally edited; tokens and calls per episode), checked by a blind double-label sample. No arm is scored here (no bake-off). This bead also owns jev-kvcc's unfinished preregistered post-rollout census and the live find-first line that rollout left in ~/.agents/AGENTS.md (jev-kvcc folds here).
WHY: N3 blocked on X6 while X6 trains on N3's DEV episodes and scores N3's HELD episodes, which N3 itself created: a circular data dependency (converge r4 fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:23; Joshua decision 8 splits N3 into N3a episodes+labels and N3b bake-off). DP-13 (locate with find vs grep vs glob) is 21,008 of the route family's 44,086 occurrences in 14 d; the other 23,078 are DP-16 ask the human 286, DP-3 prompt stage 17,449, DP-17 web vs local 3,448 and DP-6 plan first 1,895 (work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 1 row 4), with 1,250 find->read labels on DP-13. jev-kvcc's rollout of a machine-wide find-first rule is still live with a '~9x fewer tokens' claim, and its bar fixed before rollout (jev-kvcc comment 1242) was never computed: the supersede comment judged it on the description's >= 40% draft bar and the 14-day 12.7% figure (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:22, :50, :110; fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:69).
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 1 row 4 and section 3 N3; work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/decision-points.jsonl (DP-13); work/jev-04q2/measure.py; work/jev-kvcc/baseline-20261001.json (kvcc baseline, commit ea978ce1).
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/route-locate/PREREG.md, work/route-locate/episodes.py, work/route-locate/test_episodes.py, work/route-locate/EPISODES.md.
1. PREREG.md is committed before any episode is labelled and before any arm is scored here, in X6 or in N3b: the episode definition, dev/held splits by session (no session in both), the locating-tool label, the primary metric (tokens per locate episode; calls per episode secondary), the bar for N3b (an arm wins if its held tokens per episode is below both the R rule's and the grep-always arm's by a stated margin, with a paired bootstrap 95% interval excluding 0), the blind-label kappa threshold, and for each paid or local arm a max calls and max USD that X6 and N3b obey. This bead loads no model; X6 and N3b run every local-model batch behind `scripts/local-model-guard.sh --timeout 1` and record NOT_RUN on exit 2 or 3.
2. `nice -n 10 python3 work/route-locate/episodes.py --json` (it reads N0's task file) prints the DP-13 decision count beside the 44,086 route-family total, episode counts per split, the locating-tool label distribution, and the grep-always arm on the primary metric (held tokens per episode); the .776 grep share is printed as a decision share only, never as a value of the metric.
3. Planted negatives: `python3 -m unittest work/route-locate/test_episodes.py -v` asserts that an episode whose finally edited file never appears in a locate result is NOT_COUNTED (never labelled), that a session present in both dev and held makes the run refuse, and that a label row carrying raw query text is refused (hashes only).
4. Blind check: two non-author labellers label the locating tool on >= 50 sampled held episodes; Cohen's kappa against the mechanical label goes in EPISODES.md; below the PREREG threshold the label is withdrawn and N3b reports UNMEASURED.
5. KVCC CENSUS (folded from jev-kvcc; the 7-day post-rollout window 2026-10-03T19:31Z to 2026-10-10T19:31Z had not elapsed when this was written, and nothing here claims it passed): after the window closes, `nice -n 10 python3 work/jev-04q2/measure.py --by-repo --since 2026-10-03T19:31:00Z --days 7 --json` (this bead adds --by-repo and --since) computes fleet find share of locate calls, tokens per located file and combined located rate, compared with work/jev-kvcc/baseline-20261001.json (find share 7.3%, 4,631.2 tokens per located file, rate 0.342; jev-kvcc comment 1244) against the bar fixed before rollout (jev-kvcc comment 1242: find share up >= 5 pp, tokens per located file down >= 10%, located rate not down > 3 pp). EPISODES.md records PASS or FAIL per criterion. Planted negative: judging kvcc against the >= 40% draft bar or the 14-day DP-13 window is refused.
6. LIVE RULE: on that verdict, the 'Searching' line in ~/.agents/AGENTS.md keeps its find-first advice with the measured number in place of '~9x fewer tokens', or is removed; if omp-kit owns that file the change goes UPHILL to omp-kit and its bead id is recorded in EPISODES.md. The line must not keep an unmeasured number after this bead closes.
A non-author re-runs 2-3; close with commit:<sha>.

title: Ship rank: wire the bake-off winner into its host tool, L3 both ways, value receipt, KEEP/KILL
description:
WHAT: the ship step for the `rank` decision family (top `find` hit; work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:219). Once its bake-off (the organic rank bake-off inside jev-b35c.16) commits a RECEIPT naming a winning arm, wire that arm, through its cohort A adapter (jev-b35c.16) and behind its decision contract kit/contracts/rank.json, into its host tool: omp `find` ranking: .omp/hooks/post/jev-find-rank.ts and the native judge role (inventory id find); a change to omp's native find code goes UPHILL. Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. When the receipt names no winner (REFUTED, DROPPED-UNLABELLED, or no arm beat the incumbent) nothing is wired: the bead records NOT-SHIPPED with that receipt and closes. A rule arm that wins ships the same way with zero model calls. Labels: 421 organic touched-hit labels; the organic rank bake-off runs inside jev-b35c.16 (work/rank/RECEIPT.md), FiQA is a public row only.
WHY: converge r4 (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:87, fresh-conductor-c.jsonl:1) found no bead that takes a winning family arm into a host tool and produces its L3 and value receipts, so stage 1 (jev-uzq1) could close with every family CODE, REFUTED or DROPPED and none in a tool, against the mission's 'proven live' (ROADMAP.md mission line and 'Done for a feature'). Joshua decision 2 (converge r4): one P0 ship-winner bead per family that has or will have labels, which jev-uzq1 depends on.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/ship/rank/SHIP.md, kit/test/ship-rank.test.mjs.
1. `node --test kit/test/ship-rank.test.mjs` passes keylessly with injected backends against the copy the host loads: the wired arm acts on a committed real positive fixture and stays quiet on a planted negative; with the off switch set it makes zero classifier calls and the host turn proceeds; with the backend down, slow or capped it takes the contract's safe side within the latency budget. Planted negatives: a wiring that ignores the off switch fails; a host file that imports or calls askJev directly instead of going through the seam fails; a wiring attempted with no RECEIPT naming a winning arm is refused. (UPHILL: the test pins the contract the omp-kit change must meet.)
2. Both ways L3: after the expected.json row is added, jev-grzn's harness (work/l3-receipts/run.py, created by jev-grzn) writes a positive and a planted-negative receipt for this surface with session file path, log row, answering model id and spend; a FAIL turns the surface OFF, never left ON.
3. Value: jev-mvvh's ledger prints a row for this surface with verdict KEEP, PROMOTE or KILL and its reason; the value receipt is a KEEP or PROMOTE row; on KILL the off switch is flipped and a fresh session writes zero rows for the surface.
4. work/ship/rank/SHIP.md records the bake-off RECEIPT path and winning arm, the host path and off switch, the L3 receipt rows, the ledger row and the KEEP/PROMOTE/KILL verdict; or NOT-SHIPPED with the receipt that refuted, dropped or found no winner; or UPHILL with the omp-kit bead id. jev-uzq1 reads this file for the family's verdict.
5. A non-author re-runs 1-3; close with commit:<sha>.

title: Resume-quality A/B: Jev-prune vs generic summary
description:
WHAT: Run the resume-quality A/B that decides whether Jev-pruning beats generic summarization on real omp traffic.
WHY: Step 1 proved size reduction (45%) with zero text loss, but reduction is not the claim — better-than-summary continuation is. Without this test a smaller context that answers worse would ship as a win.
APPROACH:
1. Corpus: compaction/fixtures/omp-session-big-20260917.jsonl via compaction/src/omp-adapter.ts. Arm A context = compactMessages() output (see compaction/runs/replay-big-20260917.json; re-derive, do not trust it).
2. Extract the 5 dropped call ids (dump decisions with a tsx one-liner against the real Jev client) and author 3 resume questions answerable ONLY from dropped results, with expected answers quoted from the fixture.
3. Arm B context: one generic condensation of the same transcript (fixed prompt, recorded in receipt; `omp -p`, default model).
4. Resume: one fresh model call per arm, identical prompt (context + questions). Record answers verbatim. Grade substring-match against expected.
BUDGET: ~4 live calls total (Arm A re-derive 1, summary 1, resume 2). State each call in the receipt.
NON-GOALS: No library changes. No new fixtures from other sessions. No prompt-tuning to make an arm win.
ACCEPTANCE: compaction/runs/ab-<date>.json with both contexts' byte sizes, both answer transcripts, per-question grades, and a one-line verdict (A wins / B wins / tie). Verdict must be reproducible from the receipt alone.
RECEIPT: The runs/ab JSON + close reason citing it. Report model names, Jev request count, and TYPESAFE_API_KEY sourcing (env only, never in tree).
close_reason: Receipt compaction/runs/ab-20260917.json; live verdict B wins (A 1/3, B 3/3), four live calls, commit e763fa3.
