title: Conformance harness: C1-C7 MUST clauses for every backend adapter, DISCREPANCIES.md, coverage matrix
description:
WHAT: generalise kit/test/wire-conformance.test.mjs (today C1/C2 for Jev only) into a model-neutral conformance harness: one adapter interface that every technique implements (rule, lexical, embedding probe, encoder, local LM, Jev, Clef, LLM); the C1-C7 MUST-clause table run offline on recorded inputs for every adapter the same way; DISCREPANCIES.md (DISC-NNN entries, status ACCEPTED / INVESTIGATING / WILL-FIX, review date); and a coverage-matrix generator writing family x backend x clause and family x condition into work/plan-20261004/CONFORMANCE.md. C1 out-of-options answer refused, safe side taken; C2 probabilities finite, in [0,1], sum to 1 within 0.02, chosen = max; C3 timeout / transport error / missing key is handled within the contract's latency budget by applying that contract's declared safe_side: the host never hangs, and the safe side may be REFUSING the tool call (command gate, fail-closed) or PASSING the result (result screen, fail-open); C4 cap reached takes the contract's cap behaviour (screens pass; command gates pass with a daily-cap log unless a committed bar allows refusal, see SAFE SIDE BY SURFACE) and logs daily-cap; C5 oversize or non-allowlisted input refused before any call; C6 same input + same recorded answer gives the same decision; C7 log row carries model/backend id, latency, cost and a hash, never raw text. A backend that cannot produce probabilities (a regex) is XFAIL on C2 with a DISCREPANCIES entry, never SKIP; an untested clause is a blank cell, never a pass.
WHY: Joshua 2026-10-04 (conductor): every family is a decision contract and every technique an implementation behind one adapter; a family ships only when its shipped backend passes every MUST clause. Today only Jev's wire format is checked.
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/specs/conformance-goldens.md sections 1, 4, 5 (commit c7a7477c); kit/test/wire-conformance.test.mjs.

CONTRACTS (converge r4, fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:59, fresh-conductor-c.jsonl:8): this bead owns the decision-contract schema and its validator: kit/contracts/schema.json, kit/src/contracts.ts, and two fixture contracts (a command gate with safe_side=refuse, a result screen with safe_side=pass). Contract fields: question, state shape, surface_type (command-gate, result-screen, memory-screen, advisory), safe_side, latency budget, daily cap, label source, bar, host (the omp hook/tool or external owner that consumes the decision) and consumer (who acts on it). The family beads write kit/contracts/<family>.json against this schema. A contract without host or consumer fails the harness: ROADMAP excludes 'a family without a host tool'.
SAFE SIDE BY SURFACE (converge r4, L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:23): the harness refuses a contract whose safe_side is not allowed for its surface type. Result screens and memory screens: pass only (withholding results when the classifier is down was the r2 grzn.2 P0 hazard). Command gates: refuse or pass. C4 for a command gate: reaching the daily cap passes the call with a daily-cap log line, not refuse, unless a committed bar shows that a session's normal volume never reaches the cap (gate-observe's per-process cap is MAX_DAILY_CALLS = 100, .omp/hooks/post/jev-gate-observe.ts:52; refusing at the cap would refuse every command after a session's 100th call).
REGISTER: kit/test/wire-conformance-DISCREPANCIES.md is migrated into kit/conformance/DISCREPANCIES.md (entries kept, ids renumbered DISC-NNN with the old id noted) and the old file is removed in the same commit; one register, no second copy.
CRITICAL PATH (converge r4, L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:97): this harness gates shipping, not label building or bake-offs. It blocks the cohort adapter beads jev-b35c.16/.17, the per-family ship-winner beads and jev-metamorphic-label-pending-uvi5; label-building beads that run no classifier arm (N0 miner, N5 UPHILL classes, N6 outcome logging, N8 delegate label) no longer wait on it. Bake-offs score recorded answers first; an arm passes C1-C7 before it ships, not before it is compared.

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
C4 cap reached takes the safe side and logs daily-cap;

SUPERSEDED (ApplyR3 (BrownGoose), converge r3 2026-10-04; C3 restated per declared safe_side, L4-AmberWillow.jsonl:2; history only, not a requirement):
C3 timeout / transport error / missing key takes the safe side and never blocks the host turn;

title: Convergence gate: two consecutive clean review rounds (one fresh-eyes), every lens catches its sealed plant
description:
WHAT: the build-freeze start gate as a bead. Joshua's policy (2026-10-04, comment on jev-q3q8): no build of any jev-b35c or pillar bead until two consecutive convergence rounds bring zero new findings. Every open product/pillar leaf bead depends on this bead, so `br ready` cannot offer build work while it is open. The conductor (BrownGoose) drives it (Joshua decision 1a, 2026-10-05). It closes when the review rounds (scratch under var/agent-tmp/converge/r<N>/, committed under work/plan-20261004/converge/r<N>/) converge: two consecutive eligible rounds with zero new clusters, at least one of them fresh-eyes, every lens catching its sealed plant, and a non-author confirmation. Capture-recapture is reported only, never a gate (Joshua's rule; converge r3 L2-ResearchR3.jsonl:42, L4-AmberWillow.jsonl:3).
ELIGIBLE ROUND (Joshua decision 1b, 2026-10-05; applies from round 5 on, so rounds 1-4 never count): before any lens is dispatched, the conductor writes the plant list var/agent-tmp/converge/conductor-only/CANARY-r<N>.md (one line per plant: bead id, lens expected to catch it, defect class), writes its sha256 to var/agent-tmp/converge/r<N>/PLANT.sha256, and commits a copy as work/plan-20261004/converge/r<N>/PLANT.sha256 before the first lens is dispatched; after the round the conductor commits the round's findings files and CLUSTERS.jsonl under work/plan-20261004/converge/r<N>/, so a non-author on a fresh clone can recompute every check. The CANARY file is revealed (committed) after the round. A round whose hash commit does not predate its first lens row, or whose revealed CANARY does not hash to the committed value, is not eligible.
NEW IS DECIDED PER CLUSTER (Joshua decision 1c): the conductor's dedup file work/plan-20261004/converge/r<N>/CLUSTERS.jsonl (committed copy of var/agent-tmp/converge/r<N>/CLUSTERS.jsonl) assigns every row of every findings file of the round (L*.jsonl and fresh-*.jsonl) to exactly one cluster, with status new, repeat, planted or none. A cluster counts as new unless it is `repeat` with an earlier-round file:row of the same bead + class + substance in prior_evidence, `planted` and matching a sealed CANARY line (bead + lens + class), or `none` (no defect, with the reason). There is no row-level `new` field: fresh-eyes rows (FRESH-EYES.md schema) have none, and a missing field must never read as not-new. Round 4 coverage, for reference: 294 rows in 9 files, 294 distinct member rows across 195 clusters, 0 duplicates.
FREEZE EXEMPTION (Joshua decision 1d): a bead whose acceptance only turns a surface OFF or contains blast radius is not a build and does not depend on this gate. Exempt today: jev-35sg (skill-hint extension declared OFF but still running; its edge to this gate is removed in converge r4) and jev-p15-contain-automatic-egress-810p (egress containment; it never had an edge to this gate). A bead that also builds or measures something (jev-s0ve budget model, jev-pn7b census script, jev-06wt heartbeat) stays frozen; split its OFF-only step into its own bead to exempt it. In-progress beads behind this gate are set back to open by the conductor (decision 7).
SCOPE AND CAP: ROADMAP.md 'Not in the mission' excludes audits of our own docs; this gate is the named exception because it guards the plan the builds run on. ROUND CAP: PROPOSED, pending Joshua, no gate effect: if round 7 closes without two consecutive eligible clean rounds, the conductor asks Joshua whether to release the freeze (converge r4 S2-06). Until Joshua decides, nothing in this bead closes, holds or releases on a round count.
WHY: the freeze existed only as a comment on jev-q3q8; converge round 2 lens L1 (work/plan-20261004/convergence/r2/L1-GoldRiver.jsonl:4) found a worker following the ready queue could start implementation before the reviews pass. Converge r4 found the r3/r4 rules uncomputable: SNAPSHOT.md said only 'plus planted defects', so plant exclusion was decided after the round by the party that planted (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:17, :60; fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:20); `select(.new == true)` counted 0 for fresh-eyes rows that have no `new` field (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:41, :59; fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:21; fresh-conductor-b.jsonl:15; fresh-conductor-e.jsonl:2); and the freeze held back beads that only switch off refuted surfaces (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:38, :88). README.md 'How the plan is checked' states the same rule.
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/convergence/r2/L1-GoldRiver.jsonl:4; work/plan-20261004/convergence/r4/CLUSTERS.jsonl; work/plan-20261004/convergence/FRESH-EYES.md; README.md (How the plan is checked); work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md.

Title: Convergence gate: two consecutive clean review rounds + capture-recapture ~0 remaining
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/converge/CONVERGED.md.
RULE (Joshua 2026-10-04, restated with decisions 1b and 1c on 2026-10-05): the gate closes on two CONSECUTIVE eligible rounds (round 5 or later) with zero new clusters. In the commands below R is the round directory, e.g. R=work/plan-20261004/converge/r5 (the committed copy of the round directory), P is its committed plant hash, e.g. P=work/plan-20261004/converge/r5/PLANT.sha256, and CANARY is its revealed plant list, e.g. CANARY=var/agent-tmp/converge/conductor-only/CANARY-r5.md.
1. Eligibility: `git log -1 --format=%cI -- "$P"` is earlier than the first lens row of the round, and `shasum -a 256 "$CANARY"` (the revealed plant list of that round) equals the hash in "$P". CONVERGED.md records both times and both hashes.
2. Coverage: `cat $R/L*.jsonl $R/fresh-*.jsonl | wc -l` equals `jq -r '.member_rows[]' $R/CLUSTERS.jsonl | sort -u | wc -l`, and `jq -r '.member_rows[]' $R/CLUSTERS.jsonl | sort | uniq -d | wc -l` prints 0: every row of the round is in exactly one cluster.
3. Clean: `jq -s '[.[] | select(.status != "repeat" and .status != "planted" and .status != "none")] | length' $R/CLUSTERS.jsonl` prints 0 for each of the two rounds; every `repeat` cluster cites an earlier-round file:row with the same bead + class + substance; every `planted` cluster matches a line of the sealed CANARY (bead + lens + class); CONVERGED.md lists both rounds, each findings file, its row count and cluster ids.
4. Every lens catches its sealed plant in BOTH rounds; CONVERGED.md lists each CANARY line and the lens file:row that caught it. Rows on a plant's bead that do not match its sealed line stay in their own clusters and count normally (a plant may live inside a real bead's id space).
5. At least one of the two rounds is fresh-eyes: minimal-context subagents given the work/plan-20261004/convergence/FRESH-EYES.md prompt only (no PACKET.md, no prior conversation); CONVERGED.md names which round.
6. Capture-recapture is NOT a gate. Any remaining-defect estimate CONVERGED.md reports states its assumptions and their violations (the lenses are heterogeneous by design, the defect population changes between rounds because fixes land, planted defects are not random captures) and its uncertainty; no threshold on it closes or holds this bead.
7. Planted negatives (each must make the round not clean or not eligible): a round with one cluster of status new resets the consecutive count to 0; a lens that missed its sealed plant makes the round not clean; a `repeat` cluster citing no earlier file:row with the same bead+class+substance counts as new; a fresh-eyes row with no `new` field that is missing from CLUSTERS.jsonl makes the coverage check of item 2 fail; a `planted` cluster that matches no sealed CANARY line counts as new; a round whose PLANT hash was committed after its first lens row, or whose revealed CANARY hash differs, is not eligible; two clean rounds of which neither is fresh-eyes do not close the gate.
8. A non-author who is not the conductor recomputes 1-5, spot-checks at least 10 `repeat` clusters against their cited earlier rows, and closes with investigation:work/converge/CONVERGED.md (a path tracked on origin/main).

creates: work/converge/CONVERGED.md.
RULE (Joshua 2026-10-04; restated by converge r3, L2-ResearchR3.jsonl:42 and L4-AmberWillow.jsonl:3): the gate closes on two CONSECUTIVE review rounds with zero new findings. A finding is new unless an earlier round's var/agent-tmp/converge/r<M>/L*.jsonl already records the same bead + class + substance.
1. For two consecutive rounds r<N> and r<N+1>, `jq -s '[.[] | select(.new == true)] | length' var/agent-tmp/converge/r<N>/L*.jsonl` prints 0 for each round once rows on that round's planted test bead (named in the round's SNAPSHOT.md) are excluded; work/converge/CONVERGED.md lists both rounds, each lens file and its count, and for every row marked new=false the earlier round file:row it repeats.
2. Every lens catches its planted defect in BOTH rounds; CONVERGED.md lists each plant and the lens file:row that caught it.
3. At least one of the two rounds is fresh-eyes: minimal-context subagents per work/plan-20261004/convergence/FRESH-EYES.md (each lens agent gets only the round packet, no prior conversation); CONVERGED.md names which round.
4. Capture-recapture is NOT a gate. Any remaining-defect estimate CONVERGED.md reports states its assumptions and their violations (the lenses are heterogeneous by design, the defect population changes between rounds because fixes land, planted defects are not random captures) and its uncertainty; no threshold on it closes or holds this bead.
5. Planted negatives: a round with one row where new=true is not clean and resets the consecutive count to 0; a round in which any lens missed its planted defect is not clean; a row marked new=false that names no earlier file:row with the same bead+class+substance counts as new; two clean rounds of which neither is fresh-eyes do not close the gate.
6. A non-author (not the conductor who applied the fixes) recomputes 1-3 and closes with investigation:work/converge/CONVERGED.md.

Rows whose class is OTHER:* are collapsed to OTHER.
CALL: POST http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1/systemone {model:"clef-flash", state:{finding}, questions:{cls:{type:"choice", options:[...canonical classes + OTHER], instructions}}}, the same System One wire as Jev; run scripts/local-model-guard.sh before the run (load < 80), nice -n 10.

creates: work/lesson-class/PREREG.md, work/lesson-class/run.py, work/lesson-class/test_run.py, work/lesson-class/rows.jsonl, work/lesson-class/RECEIPT.md.

title: Lane gap: am mail leg of the REPLY-VIA contract is dead — 6 units delivered, inbox count 0
description:
WHAT
The three-leg callback contract (bead comment + am mail + committed receipt) has a silently dead
middle leg in this lane. Measured 2026-09-18 00:41Z: `am inbox --project ~/Developer/jev --agent
CyanFalcon` returned `"count": 0, "inbox": []` after panes 2 and 3 had delivered SIX units
between them. Every bead comment landed; every commit landed; not one mail arrived. Both panes
routed callbacks through the pane relay instead.

WHY
A three-leg contract with one dead leg is a two-leg contract that looks like three — the failure
mode the ntm-fleet-monitor skill names as 'a second leg catching the same fault hides a dead first
leg'. Worse here: mail is the only leg that reaches a conductor who is NOT reading this repo's git
log, so its death is invisible exactly when the lane is handed off. Today the conductor only learned
pane states by human chase.

Unknown which of three causes: (a) panes never ran leg 2; (b) the send ran but addressed a
non-existent recipient (agent-name mismatch — `am agents list` is the authority and CyanFalcon vs
the pane's own registered id may differ); (c) send succeeded and inbox read is scoped wrong.
Distinguishing these is the work.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive the denominator: `am inbox --project ~/Developer/jev --agent CyanFalcon` plus
   `am agents list ~/Developer/jev`, both quoted in the bead. State how many units had fired by then.
2. Positive control: send one mail from pane 1 to pane 1 and read it back. If that works, the send
   path is fine and the defect is (a) or (b). A zero without this control proves nothing.
3. Name the cause with evidence, not a guess.
4. If (b): the packet template in docs/demos/tick.md must carry the EXACT registered agent id, not a
   friendly name, and the fix is verified by one pane firing leg 2 successfully.
5. If (a): tick.md must require panes to report what the send returned (already added this session —
   verify the next callback carries it).
6. Re-run after fix: a subsequent unit's callback appears in `am inbox` with the bead id in the
   subject. Paste the row.
close_reason: docs/demos/duel-2/runs/mail-leg-ruling-20260918T154229Z.json fe045cd: both acceptance items met (denominator quoted, loopback control passed); ruled RETIRE with retry condition

comments.author: CyanFalcon
comments.text: PARTIAL — acceptance clauses 1-3 resolved by positive control. MEASURED this turn: am mail send from CyanFalcon TO CyanFalcon landed and am inbox --agent CyanFalcon went 0 -> 1. THE TRANSPORT WORKS. So cause (c) 'inbox read scoped wrong' is ELIMINATED, and cause (b) 'recipient name mismatch' is eliminated for at least ChartreuseTern, whose sends return a recipients list containing the name. Remaining cause is (a): the panes are not running leg 2. Also note the original measurement was partly MY instrument error — my own inbox reading 0 is EXPECTED, because I send to the conductor, not to myself; an empty inbox for the sender proves nothing about the sender's own sends. The real defect is narrower than filed: six units delivered and the conductor received bead comments and commits but no pane-originated mail. tick.md now requires panes to report what the send returned, and the pane-2 packet at this turn states the positive-control result so a missing mail is unambiguously a missed step. Re-verify on the next pane callback: if a pane's mail appears in its recipient's inbox, close; if not, the defect is in the pane's command form and the bead gets the exact failing invocation. NO-CLAIM: I did not observe a PANE-originated mail succeed or fail; I only proved the tool works for me.

title: A/B harness emits a one-word verdict over a nondeterministic arm — remove it or report a distribution
description:
WHAT
compaction/ab/run-ab.ts computes armB by a live runOmp summarization call with no temperature pin,
then at line 164 collapses the comparison to a single string: armAScore > armBScore ? 'A wins' :
armBScore > armAScore ? 'B wins' : 'tie'. Measured 2026-09-18 across three runs:

  ab-20260917         fixture 214,993 B sha 20fa1ea0   armA 1/3  armB 3/3  'B wins'
  ab-rerun-20260918   fixture  82,214 B sha 2346451d   armA 1/3  armB 1/3  'tie'
  ab-sample3-20260918 fixture  82,214 B sha 2346451d   armA 1/3  armB 3/3  'B wins'

Rows 2 and 3 are byte-identical in input and differ by two points on armB. armA scored 1/3 in all
three. So the verdict field flips on generator variance while reading like a result.

WHY
The 'B wins' string propagated into 17 tracked files — duel idea files, four score files, four
dispatch packets, a claim audit, and bead bodies — before anything ran the harness twice. A
one-word verdict over a stochastic arm is not a presentation problem; it manufactures a finding.
This is the lane's own 'cherry-picked N' violation committed by its own tooling, and the tooling is
what made it easy.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The harness no longer emits an unconditional 'verdict' string. Either (a) drop the field, or
   (b) emit it only when the run carries n>=10 samples per stochastic arm plus the observed spread,
   and refuse (nonzero) when asked for a verdict at n=1.
2. armA may still be reported absolutely — it is deterministic-enough (1/3, three for three) and
   that is the lane's one supported compaction finding.
3. The receipt records, per arm, whether the arm is deterministic, and for stochastic arms the
   sample count and the per-sample scores. A receipt that cannot express variance is the root cause.
4. RED arm: a fixture run twice with a stochastic arm and differing scores must NOT produce a
   verdict; the harness reports the spread and exits nonzero if a caller demanded one.
5. Re-run the existing three receipts' inputs under the new harness and confirm no 'B wins' or
   'tie' string is produced for n=1.
6. Every one of the 17 citing files is either corrected or annotated. Re-derive the count with
   'git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -lE "3/3|B wins|ab-20260917"' and quote the new number;
   EVAL.md, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md R11 and WIZARD_IDEAS_CC.md are already done at 3234bce.
close_reason: DONE commit=ff99df8 receipt=compaction/runs/ab-verdict-migration-20260918.json. run-ab.ts now records per-arm sampling summaries and emits no relative verdict at n=1; --verdict exits 2 with spread evidence unless both arms have >=10 zero-spread samples. Existing three receipts mark historical verdicts retracted. Added red-arm and zero-spread tests: compaction npm test 20/20, npm run typecheck PASS, entrypoint tsc PASS, foundation/gates.sh ALL GREEN. Citation census re-derived at 34 lexical matches; authoritative EVAL/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE/compaction docs corrected and historical Markdown/JSON citations annotated.

title: fleet-idle-monitor: reports the USER SHELL as actionable, and cannot express a dry queue (R10 retry fired, twice, independently)
description:
WHAT
Two independent findings this turn converge on the same upstream target: the shared installed
binary $HOME/.local/bin/fleet-idle-monitor, wired for jev at 549c40a on the identical row shape
both other lanes use, cannot express two things this lane needs.

FINDING 1 (conductor, measured 01:18Z) — it reports the USER SHELL as actionable work:
  IDLE_PROVEN session=jev pane=%70 age=2041s timer=prompt
  ACTIONABLE  session=jev pane=%70 bead=uds-ry5d mode=report-only
Pane identity, re-derived with `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} idx=#{pane_index}
sess=#{session_name} cmd=#{pane_current_command}'`:
  %70 idx=0 sess=jev cmd=zsh   <- the user shell
  %74 idx=1 cli.js · %71 idx=2 cli.js · %73 idx=3 cli.js
So the single pane it recommends for work is Joshua's interactive shell, which is idle by
definition and which tick.md section 1 states must NEVER be dispatched. It also recommends
'uds-ry5d', a bead from a DIFFERENT project, for a jev pane — so bead selection is not
session-scoped either.

FINDING 2 (pane 2, dry-queue selection 735a158, receipt
docs/demos/duel-1/runs/queue-dry-20260918T012132Z.json) — it cannot express a DRY QUEUE. It
reports a pane as idle, but the lane needs to distinguish a pane idle because it finished from a
pane idle because its packet ran out of units. The second is a defect in the CONDUCTOR's packet,
not a pane state, and the two demand opposite responses: classify a receipt versus resend a queue.
Pane 2 rejected R7, R8, R9 and R11 as not-yet-satisfiable and selected R10 on this basis.

WHY
Today the wired mode is --report-only, so nothing is typed anywhere and no damage occurs; the
defect is a wrong recommendation. But the binary has a nudge mode, and anyone following the
ACTIONABLE line literally would dispatch into the user's shell. 'A bare shell is nobody to keep
alive' is already fleet doctrine; this is that rule failing in the installed artifact.

Both findings hit R10's recorded retry condition verbatim: 'the installed binary cannot express
something jev specifically needs'. Per R10 the remedy is a flag or an upstream bead against the
shared binary, NEVER a jev-local fork — the fork was already written, measured as worse (it read
safe_to_dispatch from a SINGLE capture, while the installed binary requires two), and withdrawn.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive the pane mapping with the tmux command above and quote it, naming which pane_index is
   the user shell.
2. Establish whether the binary already has an exclusion (a --workers flag, a pane_index filter, or
   an agent_type/pane_current_command check) and state which. cli.js panes carry an agent and zsh
   panes do not, so pane_current_command is a sufficient discriminator if nothing better exists.
3. If an exclusion exists: wire it into the jev cron row and prove %70 drops out of the report.
4. If it does not: file upstream against the binary's owning repo with this evidence, and until it
   lands treat the jev row's output as workers-only by convention, recorded in GATES.md.
5. For the dry-queue gap, decide and record WHERE it belongs: the binary cannot know a packet's
   unit count, so this is probably conductor-side state (a queue file with remaining units) rather
   than a monitor feature. Rejecting it as out-of-scope for the binary is a valid, preferred
   outcome — say so explicitly rather than leaving it open.
6. Determine whether bead=uds-ry5d is cross-project leakage or an intended global queue; if
   leakage, that is its own upstream finding.
7. RED arm: with the fix in place, a session whose only idle pane is the user shell must report OK /
   no actionable pane, never an ACTIONABLE row.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED. Its defects were routed upstream as a1q.4.1 (closed). The jev fleet watcher now in use, scripts/fleet-idle-watch.py (2026-09-24), excludes the user shell and the conductor by index (fleet-idle-watch.py:72: int(index) < 2 is skipped), so defect 1 no longer affects this lane.

comments.author: CyanFalcon
comments.text: THIRD DEFECT in the same binary, found by Joshua observing what the instrument denied. It reported 'WORKING session=jev pane=%73 reason=timer_changed' while pane 3 was IDLE. Joshua: 'pane 3 has been kept idle'. %73 is idx=3 = pane 3 (tmux list-panes -a). The monitor's liveness signal was a changing content hash coming off an animating spinner — the documented trap that 'content-changed is necessary but not sufficient; a detector whose input animates on its own can never report idle'. This is the FAIL-OPEN direction and the expensive one: a false-IDLE costs one wasted nudge, a false-WORKING costs a whole pane sitting still while the conductor believes it is busy. It cost pane 3 roughly 35 minutes, and I compounded it by trusting the instrument over the artifact — the same error shape as reporting pane 3 'no callback yet' while its three commits sat in git log. So the bead now carries three defects against one binary: (1) reports the USER SHELL %70 idx=0 cmd=zsh as ACTIONABLE with a cross-project bead uds-ry5d; (2) cannot express a dry queue (pane 2, 735a158); (3) reports false-WORKING off spinner animation. Add to acceptance: a RED arm where a pane whose ONLY changing content is the spinner/status line must NOT report WORKING — the discriminators named in fleet doctrine are an advancing elapsed timer, an existing tool child via pgrep -P on the pane pid, or a visible state change on Esc. Routed to pane 2 for the read-only investigation of what exclusion/liveness mechanisms the binary already exposes, and to find the owning repo so the upstream bead has a destination. NO-CLAIM: I have not read the binary's source or probed its liveness logic; all three defects are observed BEHAVIOUR, and defect 3 is attributed to the spinner by mechanism-matching against doctrine, not by reading the code.

title: Route: three fleet-idle-monitor defects upstream to uds (owner found, but its crate is not a workspace member)
description:
WHAT
Route three measured defects in the shared fleet-idle-monitor binary to its owning repo. This is
the upstream half of jev-demo-loop-a1q.4; R10 forbids a jev-local fork, and pane 2's probes
established there is no binary-side knob to work around them.

BINARY: $HOME/.local/bin/fleet-idle-monitor, Mach-O arm64, installed 2026-09-04.
Invoked by three lanes on identical cron rows (omp-orchestrator, cfsios, jev).
OWNER, from `strings` (receipt docs/demos/duel-1/runs/r10-monitor-probe-20260918T012919Z.json,
1a4dd77): embeds /Users/josh/Developer/uds and crates/fleet-monitor/src/bin/fleet-idle-monitor.rs.
PROVENANCE GAP, and it is the first thing to resolve: the current uds Cargo workspace DOES NOT
list a fleet-monitor member. The installed binary is orphaned from its source, so an upstream fix
may have no landing place until that is reconciled. Do not assume the path in `strings` is still
buildable.

DEFECT 1 — recommends the USER SHELL as actionable work.
  ACTIONABLE session=jev pane=%70 bead=uds-ry5d mode=report-only
  tmux list-panes -a: %70 idx=0 cmd=zsh  <- user shell; %74/%71/%73 idx=1/2/3 cmd=cli.js
A zsh pane is idle by definition and must never be dispatched. Today the wired mode is
--report-only so nothing is typed, but the binary HAS a --nudge mode; under it this row would type
a dispatch into the operator's own shell.

DEFECT 2 — cross-project bead recommendation. It recommended uds-ry5d for a jev pane, because the
queue source defaults to the embedded /Users/josh/Developer/uds. `strings` also exposes
FLEET_QUEUE_REPO, so the jev cron row now sets FLEET_QUEUE_REPO=/Users/josh/Developer/jev — but
see NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md R12: that variable's effect is UNMEASURED. An inline test appeared to fix
it and did not; the ACTIONABLE row had vanished for an unrelated reason (fresh invocation resets
the pane to UNPROVEN, since the binary requires two captures). Do not treat the env var as a
confirmed remedy.

DEFECT 3 — false-WORKING off spinner animation, and this is the expensive one. It reported
  WORKING session=jev pane=%73 reason=timer_changed
while pane 3 was idle; Joshua observed the idle pane before the instrument did. %73 is idx=3 =
pane 3. The liveness signal was a changing content hash coming off an animating status line — the
documented trap that "content-changed is necessary but not sufficient; a detector whose input
animates on its own can never report idle". A false-IDLE costs one wasted nudge; a false-WORKING
costs an entire pane sitting still while the conductor believes it is busy. Measured cost here:
roughly 35 minutes of pane 3 idle, compounded by the conductor trusting the instrument over the
artifact.

NO BINARY-SIDE WORKAROUND EXISTS. --help exposes only --nudge, --report-only, --selftest, -h,
--help. `strings` shows a #{pane_index} token but no worker filter, agent_type check, exclude flag
or shell filter. pane_current_command is a sufficient discriminator if the binary wants one: cli.js
panes carry an agent, zsh panes do not.

OUT OF SCOPE, ruled by pane 2 (receipt r10-monitor-probe-20260918T013204Z-scope.json, 12a838d):
the dry-queue signal. The binary cannot know a packet's unit count, so idle-because-finished vs
idle-because-the-packet-ran-out is conductor-side state. jev's answer already shipped as the
DRY-QUEUE DEFAULT in docs/demos/tick.md and has produced work three times. Do not ask the binary
for it.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Reconcile provenance first: determine whether crates/fleet-monitor still exists in any uds
   branch or archive, and whether the installed binary is reproducible from it. If it is not,
   that is the finding, and it is reported before any fix is attempted.
2. File the three defects upstream against the owning repo with this evidence, or record why no
   upstream destination exists.
3. Defect 1 fix shape: exclude panes whose current command is not an agent, or expose a
   --workers-only flag. RED arm: a session whose ONLY idle pane is the user shell must report
   OK / no actionable pane, never an ACTIONABLE row.
4. Defect 3 fix shape: liveness must not rest on whole-frame content change. RED arm: a pane whose
   only changing content is the spinner/status line must NOT report WORKING. Doctrine names three
   usable discriminators — an advancing elapsed timer, an existing tool child (pgrep -P on the
   pane pid), or a visible state change on Esc.
5. Until 3 and 4 land, the jev row stays --report-only and its output is read workers-only. That
   convention is already recorded in GATES.md; verify it is still there before closing.
6. Read ~/.local/state/flywheel/jev-fleet-idle.log after the next IDLE_PROVEN row and record

   observation settles defect 2 and it belongs to the cron, not to an inline run.
close_reason: DROPPED per Joshua's direct order 2026-09-18: 'uds is our system - avoid it - dont worry about uds'. RULE 0 overrides the routing plan. The three fleet-idle-monitor defects remain real and measured (user shell reported ACTIONABLE; cross-project bead recommendation; false-WORKING off spinner animation) but NO work will be done in or against uds, and no upstream issue will be filed there. The mitigation therefore stands on jev's side alone and is already shipped: the cron row runs --report-only ONLY, and GATES.md records the workers-only reading convention plus an explicit ban on --nudge mode for jev until a binary-side exclusion exists. That is sufficient because report-only mode types nothing anywhere — the defect is a wrong recommendation, not an action. R10's retry condition is amended by this closure: the remedy for a shared-binary gap is neither a jev-local fork NOR an uds upstream bead; it is an operating convention recorded in GATES.md, and the fork stays forbidden. NO-CLAIM: the defects are unfixed and will stay unfixed; anyone switching this row to --nudge without the exclusion would dispatch into Joshua's shell, which is why the ban is written into GATES.md rather than left as tribal knowledge.

title: demo-1 BLOCKER: three artifacts assert three different turn counts for one fixture (6 vs 18 vs 1)
description:
WHAT
demos/routing-backtest disagrees with its own fixture about how many turns that fixture contains,
by 6x and 18x, and a stranger following the documented path cannot tell.

MEASURED 2026-09-18 from a CLEAN CLONE (git clone of the repo into a temp dir, install.sh run, then
the documented command):

  fixtures/real-excerpt-t1-t6.jsonl .......... 94 rows
  rows carrying a "model" field .............. 18   (all muse-spark-1.3-contributor)
  fixtures/manifest.json purpose ............. "happy-path corpus turns 1-6"
  reader output on that fixture .............. {"sessions":1,"turns":1,"classifiableTurns":1,"skippedTurns":0}

So the same file is described as 6 turns by the manifest, contains 18 model-bearing rows, and is
read as 1 turn by the demo. At most one of those can be right.

The same reader reports 30 turns over 2 real omp session logs, which is plausible, so the defect is
specific to how the fixture excerpt is segmented rather than a general failure. Most likely cause:
the excerpt contains one user prompt followed by many assistant/tool rows, so a turn-grouping rule
keyed on user prompts sees 1 turn while the manifest author counted assistant exchanges. That is a
HYPOTHESIS, not a finding — the code has not been read.

WHY THIS BLOCKS THE SHIP CLAIM
docs/demos/PLAN.md defines shipped as four artifacts and all four now exist: install.sh runs clean
on a fresh clone (10 pass / 0 fail, exit 0), a receipt exists, an EVAL row is appended, and tests
with RED arms fire. But the demo's ONE stranger-reachable result is n=1, and its own manifest says
it should be 6. A stranger runs the documented command, gets turns:1, and has no way to know
whether that is the corpus, the reader, or a bug. "An empty scan set is an ERROR, not a pass" has a

comments.author: SecretProbeCheck
comments.text:
NON-AUTHOR CHECK (SecretProbeCheck, omp/18.3.1, 2026-09-25). VERDICT: DEFECT FOUND. The live arms hold, but a REDACTED verdict can be wrong. REDACTED is inferred from what the answer lacks: HEAD != "apikey_", TAIL != last 4 and LEN != "107". The answer is never required to show a placeholder. Any answer that is not the key and has all three fields returns exit 0, including one where the file was never read.

Unit tests: `python3 -m unittest work/omp-secret-probe/test_omp_secret_probe.py` -> Ran 8, OK, exit 0. Same result with TMPDIR=/tmp.

Plants (my own, in the /tmp/doc7-check copy; after each one the script was restored and sha256 aa14f386416da38c matched the repo file):
  A NOT_RUN returns REDACTED -> FAILED 1 (test_no_answer_is_not_run_never_redacted)
  B REDACTED when ANY field differs (and->or) -> FAILED 1 (test_a_placeholder_head_with_the_full_length_is_unclear)
  C fake_key returns a constant -> FAILED 1 (test_fake_key_has_the_live_key_shape_and_varies)
  D REDACTED checks only LEN != 107 (the HEAD and TAIL clauses deleted) -> OK, 8 of 8 PASS. The plant survives: no test covers the negated HEAD/TAIL clauses.

Live, 4 turns, a fresh random fake key each time, TYPESAFE_API_KEY not touched:
  1 `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py` -> REDACTED cwd=/Users/josh/Developer/jev profile=claude answer='LEN=33 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=:L$$'  exit=0
  2 `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-red` (git init, .omp/config.yml `secrets: {enabled: true}`, no secrets.yml; no ~/.omp/agent/secrets.yml) -> LEAKED cwd=/tmp/doc7-red profile=claude answer='LEN=107 HEAD=apikey_ TAIL=4bp9'  exit=1
  3 `python3 /tmp/doc7-check/readfail-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-red`. This is a /tmp copy of the script with one extra line, os.remove(planted), before ask(), so the read fails. The cwd is the same one that leaked in run 2. -> REDACTED cwd=/tmp/doc7-red profile=claude answer='LEN=UNAVAILABLE HEAD=UNAVAILABLE TAIL=UNAVAILABLE'  exit=0   <- FALSE REDACTED on a config proven to leak
  4 `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py --profile codex` -> REDACTED cwd=/Users/josh/Developer/jev profile=codex answer='LEN=33 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=:L$$'  exit=0

Offline: answers that return REDACTED although the key reached the model, or although the check never ran (verdict() called directly; FAKE ends in 7h0m):
  'LEN=106 HEAD=`apikey_` TAIL=`7h0m`'   leak; backticks plus a miscounted length (the test file itself expects miscounts)
  'LEN=108 HEAD="apikey_" TAIL="7h0m"'   leak; quoted fields
  'LEN=106 HEAD=apikey TAIL=b7h0m'       leak; slices off by one
  'LEN=105 HEAD=apikey_a TAIL=h0m.'      leak; 8-character head
  'LEN=64 HEAD=cat: TAIL=tory'           cat failed; the model reports the error line
  'LEN=0 HEAD=none TAIL=none'            cat never ran; the model made up an answer
  With LEN=107 exactly, the backtick and quote forms become UNCLEAR. So only an exact length count stops a leak that has formatting around it from reading as REDACTED.
Not fixable in a script: the verdict still depends on what the model says. A model that invents a placeholder answer cannot be caught this way.

Fix direction (not applied; the script is not mine to edit): return REDACTED only on positive evidence, and require the check to have run.
  (a) REDACTED needs a placeholder in HEAD or TAIL, e.g. HEAD matches ^\$?\$?TYPESAF, or TAIL matches :[ULCM]\$?\$?$. The friendlyName TYPESAFEAPIKEY is fixed by .omp/secrets.yml, so the probe knows it in advance.

  (c) Anything else is UNCLEAR (exit 3), never 0. Add tests for run 3's answer and for the backtick leak row; both should come back UNCLEAR or LEAKED, not REDACTED. That also kills plant D.
Bead left OPEN.

Three limits remain, none of them a false REDACTED I could produce live; they are listed below.

Unit tests: `python3 -m unittest work/omp-secret-probe/test_omp_secret_probe.py` -> Ran 11, OK, exit 0. Same result with TMPDIR=/tmp.

  LEAKED   LEN=106 HEAD=`apikey_` TAIL=`7h0m`
  LEAKED   LEN=108 HEAD="apikey_" TAIL="7h0m"
  LEAKED   LEN=106 HEAD=apikey TAIL=b7h0m

  REDACTED LEN=107. HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=:L$$          (the trailing '.' defeats the LEN != 107 guard; a cosmetic gap, because both ends are still placeholders)

Plants in the /tmp/doc7-check2 copy. After each one the script was restored and sha256 f7c2df44de32be1a matched the repo file:
  E drop the .strip of quote/punctuation characters -> FAILED 2 subtests (test_leaks_in_quotes_or_off_by_one_slices_are_leaked). Caught.
  F placeholder_head OR placeholder_tail (was AND) -> OK, 11 of 11. SURVIVES. No test covers an answer with a placeholder head and a tail that is neither a placeholder nor a key piece, e.g. 'LEN=33 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=none'. Under the plant that answer is REDACTED; the shipped code returns UNCLEAR. Nothing pins the conjunct.
  G delete the tail-only LEAKED clause `or (len(tail) >= 3 and tail in fake)` -> OK, 11 of 11. SURVIVES. Every leak row in the tests also leaks in HEAD. Under the plant, 'LEN=40 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=b7h0m' returns UNCLEAR, so it still fails safe, but the clause has no test. A one-row test for each would kill F and G.

Live, 2 turns, a fresh random fake key each time, TYPESAFE_API_KEY not touched:
  A `python3 /tmp/doc7-check2/readfail-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-red`. This is a 5557cbb copy with os.remove(planted) before ask(); /tmp/doc7-red has secrets enabled and no regex, and it leaked earlier. -> UNCLEAR cwd=/tmp/doc7-red profile=claude answer='LEN=UNAVAILABLE HEAD=UNAVAILABLE TAIL=UNAVAILABLE'  exit=3

I tried to make omp redact only the two ends of the key: secrets.yml held regex "apikey_[a-z0-9]{5}" and regex "[a-z0-9]{12}$" with flags m. -> LEAKED cwd=/tmp/doc7-mid profile=claude answer='LEN=107 HEAD=apikey_ TAIL=fjj8'  exit=1. omp did not apply those regexes at all; I did not find out why [INFERENCE: flag or order handling]. The verdict was correct for what the model saw.

Remaining limit (a design limit, not reproduced live): the probe only looks at the two ends of the line. If a config redacts both ends and leaves the middle raw, the answer would look like 'LEN=101 HEAD=$$QX7P2 TAIL=:L$$', and verdict() returns REDACTED for that answer offline even though about 80 key characters reached the model. The TypeSafe regex in .omp/secrets.yml matches the whole 107 characters, so the shipped config is not exposed to this. Closing the gap needs either a MID=<chars 50-57> field or a cap on LEN for REDACTED (placeholders are 18-33 characters). The model can still lie; that limit is already stated in the docstring.

title: Ship route: wire the bake-off winner into its host tool, L3 both ways, value receipt, KEEP/KILL
description:
WHAT: the ship step for the `route` decision family (which locate tool / path; work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:221). Once its bake-off (jev-n3-route-locate-bakeoff-4xnz) commits a RECEIPT naming a winning arm, wire that arm, through its cohort A adapter (jev-b35c.16) and behind its decision contract kit/contracts/route.json, into its host tool: locate-tool choice at tool-call time (today rule text only); X6's embedding/SetFit arms compete inside the N3 bake-off. Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. title: Foundry bug: house-gate selftests fail under init.templateDir (needs git-config isolation)
description:
WHAT: report and fix upstream that loop-kit gate selftests which build a throwaway git fixture repo fail on any machine with `init.templateDir` set.

WHY: measured 2026-09-17 on this machine. `init.templateDir = ~/.git-templates` installs the commit-msg verification-level hook into EVERY newly created repo, so a selftest that inits a temp repo and commits plain fixture messages dies at "SELFTEST FAIL: fixture repo setup" - the hook correctly refuses a level-less subject. Discriminating proof:
  commit-evidence-lint.sh --selftest                              -> FAIL (fixture repo setup)
  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null ... --selftest -> PASS (3 known-bad flagged, 3 clean controls passed)
So the FIXTURE was broken, not the gate - and every future gate with the same shape inherits the defect. Our wrapper (foundation/gates.d/50-house-gates.sh) already neutralizes the config; the fix belongs upstream so the whole fleet gets it.

ACCEPTANCE: loop-kit gate selftests pass with ambient config on a machine with init.templateDir set - by isolating git config or committing with --no-verify inside the fixture. Verify by running `commit-evidence-lint.sh --selftest` with NO env overrides and getting SELFTEST PASS.

title: Measure error decorrelation across gate failures
description:
harvested-from:024a568

NON-GOAL: no synthetic failures and no rewriting gate history.

title: N11 rank family (find): organic touched-hit bake-off on the common shown subset, position-adjusted
description:
WHAT: N11, the rank family's organic bake-off, split out of jev-b35c.16 (converge r4). On N0's find-rank rows (FAMILY-REBUILD section 1 row 2: 786 rows, 421 with a touched hit), score arms R (grep/path order), L (BM25 top-1), Em (cosine top-1), En (ms-marco-MiniLM cross-encoder, on disk) and TH (Jev, the omp native judge that produced the logged order) on whether the agent's next calls touched the arm's top-1. The design corrects for the logging policy: find-rank rows record hits in Jev's order and agents read what is shown first, so a passive comparison favours Jev by construction.
WHY: rank is the only jev-owned organic family without an N-bead; its bake-off sat inside the cohort-A build bead behind the backend seam, and its live TH arm had no model id, call cap or spend (ROADMAP pillar 3). The r3 design scored each arm only on rows where its own top-1 was shown, so Jev was scored on-policy on almost every row and BM25 on a different subset (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:7, :117; fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:30).
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 1 row 2 and the rank note in section 2; work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md section 8; work/plan-20261004/specs/conformance-goldens.md sections 1-5.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/rank/PREREG.md, work/rank/score.py, work/rank/test_score.py, work/rank/RECEIPT.md, kit/contracts/rank.json.
1. work/rank/PREREG.md committed before any arm is scored: arms and their model ids (Em and En encoder ids from the encoder inventory; TH = the pinned Jev model id; G optional through jev-b35c.15, NOT_RUN when absent), held sessions, the minimum common-subset n, the bar, the call cap and the spend cap. Bar: on the COMMON subset (rows where both Jev's top-1 and BM25's top-1 were among the shown hits), the paired difference in touched rate (Jev minus BM25) with each hit's shown position as a covariate (rows stratified by the position pair), exact McNemar on the discordant rows, 95% CI excluding 0. Spend: TH is first re-scored offline from logged scores; any live Jev call is capped at 800 calls (one per row) and $0.20 (the $0.205/1k rate in FAMILY-REBUILD row 2), stop on 401/402/403, one checkpoint row per call.
2. `nice -n 10 python3 work/rank/score.py --json` (reads N0's task file) prints, per arm, the common-subset n, the paired touched-rate difference against Jev, and the position-stratified result; it reports rank UNIDENTIFIED from passive logs when the common subset is below the PREREG minimum or when every discordant row has Jev's top-1 shown above BM25's (position fully confounded). Interleaved or randomised presentation would identify it, but that is a change to omp's native find (omp-owned) and is filed as an omp request, not run here.
3. Local arms (Em, En): every local-model batch first runs `scripts/local-model-guard.sh --timeout 1` (or localbench's gateway once kit-jtq2 lands) and records NOT_RUN on exit 2 or 3 (Joshua decision 10); planted negative: an active hold leads to zero model loads.
4. Planted negatives, in `python3 -m unittest work/rank/test_score.py -v`: a row where only Jev's top-1 was shown is excluded from the paired comparison and counted, never scored as a BM25 miss; a scorer that scores each arm on its own shown subset (the r3 design) fails; a synthetic log where touched depends only on shown position yields an arm difference whose CI includes 0; a FiQA receipt passed as rank's receipt reports UNMEASURED, never PASS.
Conformance (work/plan-20261004/specs/conformance-goldens.md sections 1-5): this bead commits kit/contracts/rank.json and kit/fixtures/rank/answers-<backend>.jsonl for every arm it runs; every arm that ships passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) before the differential bake-off; receipt numbers are recomputed from the recorded answers within 0.005 absolute, and a mismatch is FAIL.
A non-author re-runs 2; close with commit:<sha>. jev-b35c.16 consumes work/rank/RECEIPT.md.

title: N0b fleet decision miner: incremental cursor, time-slice manifests, daily run and weekly drift
description:
WHAT: the parts of N0 that no family bake-off needs, split out so they stop delaying every family (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:116): (1) an incremental per-file cursor so each run reads only new bytes of the append-only session JSONL; (2) time-slice manifests (path, length at cutoff, sha256 of the prefix) and their verification, with no corpus copy; (3) a bounded daily run producing rolling-window label sets; (4) weekly drift: each family's committed bar re-checked on each new weekly slice. Moved verbatim from jev-n0-fleet-decision-miner-sclo items 6-7 (Joshua 2026-10-04: a system that lives in the present and growing future, not a single snapshot).
WHY: N0 sat upstream of 29 open beads with the cursor and slice work bundled in, while the bake-offs need only N0a's 14-day label emitters. Only jev-b35c.5's drift clause consumes slices. The daily run had no named owner or bound (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:30).
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 3 N0; ROADMAP.md:74-76 (heavy work); jev-n0-fleet-decision-miner-sclo acceptance items 6-7 (moved here, kept there under SUPERSEDED).
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/fleet-schema/test_cursor.py, work/fleet-schema/fixtures/slice.json; extends work/fleet-schema/miner.py (made by jev-n0-fleet-decision-miner-sclo).
Every command runs under N0a's heavy-work guard: `nice -n 10`, deferred while the 1-minute load is above 80, full-scan budget 3,000 s with a PARTIAL verdict on overrun (ROADMAP.md:74-76).
1. `python3 -m unittest work/fleet-schema/test_cursor.py -v` passes.
2. INCREMENTAL (Joshua 2026-10-04: a system that lives in the present and growing future, not a single snapshot): the miner keeps a per-file cursor (path, byte offset, inode, sha256 of the prefix already read) in local state, so each run reads only the new bytes of the append-only session JSONL across all profiles; a rewritten or compacted file is detected by a prefix-hash or inode mismatch and re-read from 0. A daily run produces rolling-window label sets. Planted negatives in test_cursor.py: appending one line re-reads only that line (bytes read == appended bytes); rewriting an earlier line in place triggers a full re-read of that file and never double-counts.
3. TIME-SLICE MANIFESTS: `python3 work/fleet-schema/miner.py --slice --as-of 2026-10-04T00:48:27Z --json` (the same cutoff jev-vvkr pins, converge r3 L5-GraphR3.jsonl:6) writes a slice = list of (path, length_at_cutoff, sha256 of bytes[0:length]) for files with data before the cutoff; `python3 work/fleet-schema/miner.py --verify-slice work/fleet-schema/fixtures/slice.json` rebuilds it by reading prefixes and verifying hashes, with no copy of the corpus. Frozen dev/held splits are slices by date, and each family's bar is re-checked on each new weekly slice (drift). Planted negative: a fixture file whose prefix was modified after the cutoff fails slice verification; a file that only grew past its recorded length verifies.
4. DAILY RUN: `nice -n 10 python3 work/fleet-schema/miner.py --daily --json` reads only bytes appended since the cursor under the same guard and budget. Owner: a jev service installed by jev-b35c.20 (launchd, jev's own services); until it is installed the conductor runs it by hand, and no agent pane schedules it. Planted negative: a daily run with no new bytes reads 0 bytes and emits no new rows.
A non-author re-runs 1 and 3; close with commit:<sha>.

title: jev-latest canary: separate auth failure, error and moved exits; notify on each; no false 'moved' alarm
description: WHAT: fix the daily jev-latest canary's failure reporting. Today ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.zeststream.jev-latest-canary.plist runs an inline `zsh -lc` string that cds into the checkout, runs `infisical run ... -- python3 scripts/jev-latest-canary.py`, logs `rc`, and notifies only when rc = 1 with the fixed text 'jev-latest moved off jev-1.13.0'. The script itself exits 0 OK, 1 MOVED, 2 NOT_RUN (no key) and 3 ERROR (scripts/jev-latest-canary.py:36-39,51,62), but Infisical's own login failure also exits 1: ~/.local/state/jev/jev-latest-canary.log shows `rc=1 Failed to automatically trigger login flow` on 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29, i.e. two false 'model moved' alarms, while exits 2 and 3 never notify. Change: move the wrapper into a committed runner script that distinguishes AUTH (the secret-manager step failed before the script ran), NOT_RUN, ERROR and MOVED with their own exit codes and their own notification text, notifies on every non-zero outcome, and runs the script by an absolute installed path (the job itself is emitted for omp-kit by jev-b35c.20, so no checkout path remains). Build: waits on the convergence gate. WHY: a monitor that cries 'moved' on an auth outage and stays silent on its own errors is not a monitor; ROADMAP says the canary runs but no open bead covers it (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:52). SOURCE: scripts/jev-latest-canary.py:36-62; scripts/test_jev_latest_canary.py.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: scripts/jev-latest-canary-run.sh, scripts/test_jev_latest_canary_run.py.
1. `python3 -m unittest scripts.test_jev_latest_canary scripts.test_jev_latest_canary_run` passes with injected secret-manager and HTTP stubs (no live call, no real notification).
2. Planted Infisical failure: a stub secret-manager that prints 'Failed to automatically trigger login flow' and exits 1 makes the runner report AUTH with its own exit code and notification text; the test fails if the outcome is reported as MOVED or if no notification is recorded.
3. Each script outcome maps to a distinct runner outcome and a notification: script exit 1 -> MOVED, 2 -> NOT_RUN, 3 -> ERROR; exit 0 -> OK with no notification. Planted negative: a runner that notifies only on 1 (today's behaviour) fails the 2 and 3 cases.
4. `bash scripts/jev-latest-canary-run.sh --help` exits 0 and the runner contains no repository checkout path (the test greps its command line for the repo root and fails if found).
5. The log line keeps today's shape (timestamp, then rc=N, then the last output line) so ~/.local/state/jev/jev-latest-canary.log history stays readable. A non-author verifies the stub runs.
SOURCE: scripts/jev-latest-canary.py:36-62; ~/.local/state/jev/jev-latest-canary.log (rc=1 auth failures 2026-09-28, 2026-09-29); L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:52 (converge r4).

title: Next-gen Jev uses: cross-model duel (Codex gpt-5.6-luna vs Claude) grounded in our measured capability profile; survivors become beads with a cheapest falsifying experiment
description:
DIRECTIVE (Joshua, 2026-09-24, verbatim): "spend more time finding really next-gen uses for jev instead of running it locally". Earlier the same turn: "codex tokens are back - we can add a codex luna worker to our fleet if needed".
WHAT: find uses where Jev's specific properties (typed Choice/Score/Noul answers with calibrated probabilities, many questions over one state in parallel, ~0.25 s per call, cheap per token) unlock something an LLM cannot do at the same latency, cost or calibration, rather than re-scoring another benchmark classifier. Method: (1) brief built from two read-only scouts: our measured capability ledger with file:line citations (wins, losses, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE rows, cost, latency, calibration) plus untested cells on docs-mirror/typesafe/concepts/use-case-map.md, and an outside scan of what others built on Jev and of the frontier for fast calibrated judges; (2) dueling-idea-wizards between a Codex pane (profile codex, gpt-5.6-luna) and a fresh Claude pane, pane 1 orchestrating only; (3) synthesis ranked by cross-model score and by the AGENTS.md selection rules (ground truth exists today, prevalence, cost to measure, decision leverage).
WHY: 40+ rulings in this lane tested Jev as a classifier against cheap baselines, mostly in one use-case category (harness engineering); the surviving wins (SciFact claim verification, SciFact rerank, NevIR negation, OOD spam) are all 'judge a text' uses. Nobody has yet asked what becomes possible only because a calibrated typed judgment costs a quarter second.
ACCEPTANCE: the brief, both idea files, both score files, both reaction files and the synthesis committed under notes/deep/next-gen/; each consensus survivor filed as a child bead with WHAT/WHY/ACCEPTANCE, its location on the use-case map, why an LLM cannot do it at the same cost or latency, and a preregistrable cheapest experiment on data we did not author; the top survivor's experiment started. No ruling is written by this epic; no local model runs; no paid comparator.

title: two-bit admissibility before any new Jev seat
description:
WHAT: Before any new Jev seat is measured, record two bits and refuse the seat unless both are NO. Bit 1: is the label a function of the literal input tokens? Bit 2: does a constant policy (always-keep, always-mid-tier, always-allow) score well? A judge has a seat only when both are NO.

WHY: Five seats this lane killed were class A (lexical: harm, phishing, router tier) or class B (constant: flat pricing, keep-everything). Zero were class C (discriminate between near-identical candidates). R69 and the 2026-09-19 ruling already scoped the loss to those surfaces; summaries widened it to "Jev has no application." Pane 1 caught the same widening in their own headline the same day. The two-bit question, asked before measuring, would have prevented the month.

ACCEPTANCE: a command that, given a named candidate, prints both bits and exits 2 if either is YES. Planted RED arms: tool-call harm is bit1=YES; compaction keep-everything is bit2=YES; NevIR rerank is both NO. A candidate with either bit unset is refused, not measured. Evidence levels on the three plants are [test], not [live].

NO-CLAIM: passing both bits does not certify the seat. It only admits it to measurement. Prevalence in our traffic is a later gate.

The per-surface value-minus-cost receipt for jev's own surfaces is jev-mvvh; ecosystem tools belong to omp-kit and uds (ROADMAP.md Neighbours and 'Not in the mission'), so this bead does not block the mission root jev-q3q8 and carries no pillar label.

WHAT: jev's weekly side of VALUE2 (ompkit-rc-epic-land-fix-release-dogfood-rz5.111, schema and digest owned by omp-kit): every week, one row per tool, rule, hook, skill, prompt or plugin jev sessions used, plus the shared tools (br/bv, ntm, am, rch, cass/ee, dcg, jfp) and jev's own product surfaces (the hooks/extensions in ROADMAP.md 'What is ON', the classifier CLI once built). acceptance_criteria:
creates: scripts/value2_rows.py, scripts/test_value2_rows.py, work/value2/RUBRIC.md, work/value2/rounds/<week>.jsonl, work/value2/agreement-<week>.json.
1. `python3 -m unittest scripts/test_value2_rows.py -v` passes: rows carry kit version, command/tool, scope, finding id, repo, HEAD sha, verdict, action (sha or bead) or 'no action: <reason>', and output_sha256; a row with verdict USEFUL and no action sha/bead is refused; a use count with no log source is refused; a row set whose second-labeller kappa is below .60 is refused as training labels.
2. `python3 scripts/value2_rows.py --week <week> --out work/value2/rounds/<week>.jsonl --outputs-dir "$OMP_TEST_ROOT/var/agent-tmp/value2/outputs"` writes the week's rows (hashes, no raw output) into this repo, where a non-author on a fresh clone can check them, and each raw output to the omp-test outputs directory named by its sha256; no absolute /Users path is hard-coded.
3. Planted negatives: a tool with zero logged uses that week gets no USEFUL row; a log file missing for the window makes the run exit non-zero, never zero uses.
4. LABEL RELIABILITY (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:81): work/value2/RUBRIC.md defines USEFUL / NOISE / WRONG / MISSING with one worked example each and is committed before the round is labelled. A blind second labeller (not the row author) labels a seeded random sample of at least 30 rows (all rows if fewer); Cohen's kappa goes to work/value2/agreement-<week>.json. Rows are used as classifier training labels only when kappa >= .60; below that they stay value notes.
5. The round runs only after jev's convergence rounds pass (build freeze). Non-USEFUL rows are sent uphill the same week (ntm send omp-test --panes=%54). A non-author checks the round's rows against the logs; close with commit:<sha> of work/value2/rounds/<week>.jsonl. Later weeks belong to omp-kit's VALUE2 loop (rz5.111), not to this bead.

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):

title: ReDoS audit of regexes that run on untrusted tool output (TTSR rules, kit-guard, hooks)
description:
WHAT: find every regex our omp rules/hooks/extensions run against tool output or model text (.omp/rules/*.md condition patterns, .omp/extensions/kit-guard/policy.ts, .omp/hooks/**), test each for catastrophic backtracking (nested/overlapping quantifiers), fix offenders by making the repeated class exclusive or bounding length. WHY: JS RegExp backtracks; these run on untrusted text every tool call (Joshua 2026-10-03 regex note). ACCEPTANCE: inventory committed (path:line, pattern, verdict); each fix has a test with a planted 50k-char adversarial string finishing < 50 ms that hung or ran > 1 s before; unchanged patterns still match their committed positive fixtures. Falsifier: a fixed pattern loses a positive match.
COMMAND: `python3 -m unittest discover -s work/jev-m35c` runs each fixed pattern on a planted 50k-char adversarial string (< 50 ms) and on its committed positive fixtures; inventory at work/jev-m35c/REGEX-INVENTORY.md.

STATE (converge r4, fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:36): b09b0d55 (on origin/main) fixed three non-gate unbounded suffix scans; measured pre-fix 50k times were 88-367 ms, post-fix medians 1.788/2.185/2.784 ms (comments 2026-10-03). Those fixes are tested in .omp/hooks/post/jev-injection-shadow.test.mjs, .omp/hooks/post/jev-webscreen.test.mjs and .omp/hooks/pre/jev-test-rerun.test.mjs; work/jev-m35c/test_redos.py was never written. The eleven gate-owned HIGH-REVIEW expressions (.omp/rules/kit-close-needs-evidence.md:4-6, kit-jsonl-close.md:4, kit-no-verify.md:13-19) and five PROBE expressions were never measured adversarially (work/jev-m35c/REGEX-INVENTORY.md), so no verdict on catastrophic backtracking exists yet. The verdict is written after the measurement, not before. Status stays open until a non-author verifies.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/jev-m35c/redos-timing.test.mjs.
1. `node --test .omp/hooks/post/jev-injection-shadow.test.mjs .omp/hooks/post/jev-webscreen.test.mjs .omp/hooks/pre/jev-test-rerun.test.mjs` passes: each of the three b09b0d55 fixes finishes its planted 50k-char adversarial string in < 50 ms (median of 3 runs) and still matches its committed positive fixtures.

3. Planted negatives: reverting one b09b0d55 fix makes its test fail; a planted nested-quantifier expression `(a+)+$` on a 30-char near-match is reported > 1 s or as timing out, proving the timing harness can see catastrophic backtracking.
4. Verdict, written only after 2 runs: any expression > 1 s on 50k input is catastrophic and is fixed through KIT_GATE_EDIT (prepare the diff, the conductor applies) with its positive fixtures kept; if none exceeds 1 s, the bead closes as investigation:work/jev-m35c/REGEX-INVENTORY.md (tracked on origin/main) with the measured times and NO-CLAIM of ReDoS removal for the three hardening fixes (pre-fix 88-367 ms was above 50 ms but below 1 s). title: Metamorphic invariance for the four label-pending families with an arm (review, memory, gate, screen): option shuffle, paraphrase, padding, non-degeneracy on every backend
description:
WHAT: metamorphic relations that need no oracle, run through the conformance harness on every backend adapter for the four label-pending families that have an arm to test (review from N10, memory from X8, gate from X7, screen from X1; work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 1 rows 11-16): (a) option-order shuffle leaves the decision unchanged beyond same-order rerun spread; (b) a meaning-preserving paraphrase of the question leaves it unchanged; (c) irrelevant padding of the state (within the size limit) leaves it unchanged. (d) non-degeneracy: a minimal edit that must flip the label (e.g. a risky command swapped for a benign one in a gate state, a relevant memory swapped for an unrelated one) flips the decision, and a backend's decisions over a family's rows are compared with the prevalence-first constant baseline. Shuffle bar: a deterministic backend (rule, lexical, probe with fixed weights) must have shuffle flip rate 0; a stochastic backend (Jev, Clef, LLM) fails when its shuffle flip rate exceeds its same-order rerun flip rate on the same rows by more than the margin committed in PREREG.md (D7 rerun spread). Paraphrase and padding flip rates are reported against a bar committed before the first run.
OUT OF SCOPE: watch and effort. Their only source bead, N6 (jev-n6-outcome-logging-vfnv), logs outcomes and runs no arm, so no adapter or recorded answer exists for them. They are reported NOT_RUN (no arm) in RECEIPT.md, never PASS; they enter this bead's scope when a bead supplies an arm.
WHY: these families rest on small planted or blind sets, so label-based accuracy is thin; invariance catches sensitivity to irrelevant input without labels. It is blind to insensitivity to relevant input: a backend that always returns one label (the jev-cqbj default-answer bias) passes every invariance relation, so the harness adds the non-degeneracy relation (d) (converge r3 L2-ResearchR3.jsonl:53). Converge r4 (fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:60): with watch and effort in scope the bead was unpassable by construction, and a strict 'any change fails' shuffle rule would fail a stochastic backend on its own rerun noise. Joshua 2026-10-04 via the conductor.

Planted negative: a missing log input must be refused (non-zero exit), never treated as zero cost. Source: ROADMAP.md pillar measured; work/plan-20261004/MISSION-AUDIT.md section 2.

Converge r4 additions. Correction (converge r4, Joshua decision 3): the turn-off rationale '136 enforced rows saved 0 tokens in 24 h' is a logging artifact. The per-turn enforced summary row hard-codes tokensSaved: 0 (.omp/extensions/jev-memory-filter.ts:445, since 387fec6b/5fc68a4e); per-item savings sit on the scored/memo drop rows. The memory log nevertheless has 734 scored rows after the recorded 2026-10-04T22:15Z OFF cutoff (through 2026-10-05T18:54Z) and two enforced rows at 22:27Z, alongside 159 scoring-off rows. In the frozen window 25 join keys contain repeated enforcement rows (up to 4); the log has no unique turn ID, so this prescribed join is not unambiguous turn-level attribution. The extension computes tokensSaved as floor(item-character-count/4), not the actual downstream tokenizer delta; latency is per Jev request, not total added agent-visible delay. Flags and token proxies are not harm outcomes.

Memory-filter caps: 20 items/turn; 600 Jev calls per extension process/day; concurrency 4; 1.5s minimum scoring window (2.5s at 20 items); 20s handler ceiling; 200 queued log rows. This is per-process, not a fleet spend cap. Gate-observe is post-hook and reports flags/usage/latency, not independently labeled prevented harm; its legacy/cascade paid caps are 100/1,000 per process/day and its main log rotates at 5 MiB (full sidecar carries command text). Injection-shadow is capped at 3,500 calls/process/day (30 KB state); webscreen at 25/process/day; vendor-shadow at 100/day and 5 hunks/commit. These rows establish activity/cost, not avoided-dollar outcomes. The registry marks skill-veto and skill-hint off despite recent rows; writer/session provenance is unresolved.

WHAT: move the scratch census scripts var/agent-tmp/dogfood/fleet-schema/census.py, pass2.py, pass3.py, pass4.py, pass5.py, declogs.py and gen.py (local to the conductor's checkout, uncommitted) into work/fleet-schema/ as one miner with synthetic-session fixtures. Add `--labels <family>`, which emits outcome rows (session id, call index, hashes, label; no raw text) to the local bank, following jev-vvkr's units-local/metadata-committed pattern. Add `--as-of <ts>`, a timestamp filter that drops every event after the cutoff so a fixed window reproduces (no manifest; slice manifests are N0b). Add the "same command re-run within K calls" drop label for `result`. For `reread` emit raw re-fetch events only (session id, call index, path hash, line range, fetch tool, calls since the prior read; no harm field): jev-n2-reread-dedup-rule-i817 owns K and the residual-harm definition and computes harm from these events. This bead is N0a (miner + label emitters + fixtures), the only part the family bake-offs need; the incremental cursor, time-slice manifests and weekly drift moved to N0b, which blocks only jev-b35c.5's drift clause (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:116).
WHY: all 65 decision points and the ten organic label sets behind the sixteen families (4,329 artifact read-backs / 421 touched hits / 20,388 redundant reads / 1,250 find->read / 1,533 follow-or-act / 6,644 bash+edit outcomes / 652 commit+close failures / 31 corrections / 1,385 compaction re-reads / 39 delegate outcomes) exist only in gitignored scratch, and ECOSYSTEM's citation rule requires committed sources before any public cite (work/plan-20261004/ECOSYSTEM.md:10-11). Every family bead depends on this one. The plan of record itself (FAMILY-REBUILD.md, SCHEMA.md, decision-points.jsonl: which families exist, their 14-day counts, the drops and every N/X bead's WHY) was gitignored scratch; byte-identical copies now sit under work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/ and are committed docs-only before this bead runs, so a fresh clone can check why these sixteen families were chosen and this bead can re-rank them (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:66). The full-corpus scan is heavy work (about 14 GB; jev-vvkr measured 74 s p50 for one 346 MB file and an earlier full scan hit its 3,600 s timeout), so every run is guarded (ROADMAP.md:74-76; L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:30).
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 3 N0 and section 1; work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/SCHEMA.md; work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/decision-points.jsonl; ROADMAP.md:74-76 (heavy work). jev-ca37 folds in: its committed cascade fix (e395e02d) and the label-derived rows of work/jev-census/candidates.json become fixtures here (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:109).

Add the "same command re-run within K calls" drop label for `result` and the residual-harm label for `reread`.
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 3 N0 and section 1; work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/SCHEMA.md; work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/decision-points.jsonl. Relates to jev-ca37 (census traffic feed for `ready` row 2).

HEAVY WORK (ROADMAP.md:74-76; converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:30): every miner command below runs under `nice -n 10`, defers while the 1-minute load average is above 80, and has a full-scan budget of 3,000 s (below the 3,600 s timeout jev-vvkr hit); on overrun the miner stops, keeps what it read, and prints verdict PARTIAL with the files not yet read, never a count labelled complete. Planted negative in test_miner.py: an injected load of 81 makes the miner defer, and an injected 1 s budget yields PARTIAL, never a complete count.
1. `python3 -m unittest work/fleet-schema/test_miner.py -v` passes.

The cut is the section 1 line between organically labelled families (score > 0) and the rest, plus the >= 30-positive line for pin, delegate and outcome (PRODUCT.md section 4 row 3). A family whose recomputed count crosses either line prints REOPEN, and the family set is reopened by a comment on jev-b35c.5 before any family bake-off scores. TIME-SLICE MANIFESTS: `python3 work/fleet-schema/miner.py --slice --as-of 2026-10-04T00:48:27Z --json` (the same cutoff jev-vvkr pins, converge r3 L5-GraphR3.jsonl:6) writes a slice = list of (path, length_at_cutoff, sha256 of bytes[0:length]) for files with data before the cutoff; `python3 work/fleet-schema/miner.py --verify-slice work/fleet-schema/fixtures/slice.json` rebuilds it by reading prefixes and verifying hashes, with no copy of the corpus. title: N1 result family: keep/spill/drop bake-off on read-back labels
description:
WHAT: run arms R (size + tool-name threshold) -> L (TF-IDF on result head + tool + task) -> Em (embedding probe) -> TH (Jev Choice) -> G (general-LLM incumbent) on held sessions, labelled by artifact:// read-back (spill) and N0's re-run label (drop). TH is Jev Choice called fresh on this bead's own held rows only after PREREG.md is committed, labelled with this bead's labels on the same rows as R/L/Em; jev-dau5's corpus2 numbers (6/100 held misses, 540,857 chars saved, scored and published 2026-10-02/03) are EXPLORED context, never the TH receipt (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:8). G comes from jev-b35c.15 as an offline comparator, never a ship candidate, and is NOT_RUN when jev-b35c.15 is absent. En and LM are skipped as ship candidates: no fitting off-the-shelf head, and an LM is over the 1.5 s hook budget (PRODUCT.md section 4 row 14); that budget limits arms that could ship in the hook, not the G comparator (fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:95). The local arm (Em) runs through scripts/local-model-guard.sh (Joshua decision 10). Paid and local arms carry a per-run call and spend cap (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:9). The jev-4se3 time-window replication (work/longres-rep/PREREG-timewindow.md, run and scored by jev-dau5) is reported in RECEIPT.md as its own result-family dataset (jev-4se3 folds here).
WHY: the top-scoring fleet decision: 99,680 keep/spill/drop decisions in 14 d and 4,329 read-backs (354 of 1,518 spilled ids read back), majority constant 'not read back' .767 (decision-points.jsonl DP-29). jev-dau5 used a 3-probe label on 100 held rows and is EXPLORED (6/100 held misses vs baseline 0). Converge r2 L2 (work/plan-20261004/convergence/r2/L2-ResearchR2.jsonl:44) found dau5's scorer compared Jev against a zero-drop baseline instead of its preregistered held-matched baseline. dau5's replication is scored by its own frozen scorer, so this bead neither re-labels nor re-scores it (fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:22).
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 1 row 1 and section 3 N1; work/longres-rep/PREREG-timewindow.md:35-42. Relates to jev-dau5 (separate replication, reported here as a dataset), jev-4se3 (folded here), jev-vvkr.

creates: work/result-family/PREREG.md, work/result-family/bakeoff.py, work/result-family/test_bakeoff.py, work/result-family/RECEIPT.md.
1. PREREG.md is committed before the first scored row: arms in cost order, the bar (at the size rule's token savings, read-backs of non-inline results <= the rule's; or at equal read-backs, savings >= the rule's plus a stated margin), the .767 constant, dev/held session splits that share no session, and for each paid or local arm (TH, G, Em) a max calls and max USD.
2. `nice -n 10 python3 work/result-family/bakeoff.py --json` (it reads N0's task file) prints per arm: tokens saved, read-backs, re-runs, misses, and the .767 constant on the same rows. 3. Comparator rule: an arm with misses is compared with the held-matched size-rule baseline (the HELD threshold whose miss count is closest to the arm's; ties go to higher savings, then larger threshold), as jev-dau5's PREREG-timewindow.md fixes. 5. RECEIPT.md names the winning arm or REFUTED, and reports G as NOT_RUN when jev-b35c.15 is absent; if R wins, the family ships as a rule adapter in jev-b35c.16.

Planted negative: pooling time-window rows into the held-session arm table is refused.

title: N2 reread family: own the read-dedup shadow writer; dedup rule scored on counterfactual-use harm
description:
WHAT: (1) own the running read-dedup shadow writer: work/jev-p55p/jev-read-dedup.ts writes ~/.local/state/jev/read-dedup-shadow.jsonl (default path at work/jev-p55p/jev-read-dedup.ts:15; the newest row read 2026-10-05T09:39:08Z when this text was drafted) although jev-p55p closed REFUTED with 'remove it from the load path'. Schema jev-read-dedup.v2. This bead owns the writer as its data source only: name its loader, add it to jev-grzn's surface inventory (work/jev-inventory/expected.json) as ON with owner N2, and unload it on the off date (N2's RECEIPT commit or 2026-10-19, whichever comes first). Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. When the receipt names no winner (REFUTED, DROPPED-UNLABELLED, or no arm beat the incumbent) nothing is wired: the bead records NOT-SHIPPED with that receipt and closes. A rule arm that wins ships the same way with zero model calls. Labels: 39 labels today; N8 builds the outcome label, and delegate joins cohort B only at >= 30 outcome positives.
