title: Smart stop: 309 checks/24h, 0 continuations - find out why
description:
WHAT: omp's Jev unexpected-stop classifier ran 309 times in 24h and continued no agent (genuine 'Attempt #N/3' markers = 0). Replay on 300 real stops flagged 8/300 (2.7%), so ~8 continuations were expected. Determine which: (a) the fleet truly never promise-stops (classifier right), (b) judge says yes but omp does not continue (bug: read turn-recovery.ts ~1040-1125, check conditions after classification, e.g. RPC/interactive mode, retry budget), (c) judge says no on real promise-stops (false negatives). Method: pull the last 100 organic text-only stops that were classified (timestamps of model_usage purpose=unexpected-stop), re-ask the exact omp question live (jev-1.13.0) to get scores, hand-label blind whether each promised an action. ACCEPTANCE: per-case table (score, label, continued?), verdict among a/b/c with evidence; if (b), a minimal repro and an upstream issue draft (oh-my-pi), not a local patch. NO-CLAIM: not a benefit measure.
REALITY CHECK 2026-10-01: fleet sat idle ~6h because the ready queue was empty and every benefit question waited passively for traffic. Native Jev runs ~8,400 calls/day (find 7,137, auto-thinking 703, unexpected-stop 309, ttsr 285 in 24h) but no surface has a measured benefit. Rules: bar fixed in a bead comment BEFORE reading outcome data; live calls bounded, spend stated; non-author verifier closes; NO-CLAIM line.
WHY: smart stop made 309 checks in 24 h with 0 continuations; without a per-case table nobody knows whether the stop rule never fires or fires and is ignored (work/jev-nwo1-verdict.md:17-26).

Over-refusal risk: the recorded 7-day replay (comment 2026-10-03T17:48Z) saw 156 candidate commits, of which 147 changed results and all 147 were refused (100%); the 9 that changed no result were not refused. SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
WHAT: a commit-msg/pre-commit check: any commit that adds or changes a result row in EVAL.md or NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md, or a DONE-style result file, must also add (or reference by committed path+sha) per-call rows, the scorer and the split/seed; otherwise refuse with the missing piece named. WHY: violated at least 7 times on 2026-10-02 (R147, R149, R142, 9yjh labels, double-read, xdzh freeze hash, census crash); each cost a verifier round trip. ACCEPTANCE: gate-file change via KIT_GATE_EDIT (prepare diff, conductor applies); tests: a result row without rows is refused, with rows passes, a docs-only EVAL edit (no numbers) passes; replay the last 7 days of result commits and report how many would have been refused. Falsifier: if fewer than 2 of the 7 known cases would be caught, the rule is aimed wrong.
COMMAND: `python3 -m unittest scripts.test_result_commit_evidence` (refuse a result row without rows; pass with rows; pass a docs-only edit); gate: scripts/result_commit_evidence.py, applied through KIT_GATE_EDIT.
OVER-REFUSAL BAR (converge r2 L4, work/plan-20261004/convergence/r2/L4-HonestyR2.jsonl:17): the recorded 7-day replay refused 147 of 156 result-changing commits (94%; comment 2026-10-03T17:48Z). Before the hook is wired into pre-commit: commit a false-refusal bar (Wilson upper <= 10%); label a random 30 of the refused replay commits truly-missing vs present-elsewhere; plant a legitimate result commit that references its rows by committed path+sha, which must pass `python3 -m unittest scripts.test_result_commit_evidence`. Wire the hook only if both the miss falsifier (>= 2 of 7 caught) and the false-refusal bar hold; the 7 known incidents are the rule's training cases, so the false-refusal sample is drawn from other commits.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/jev-oh7c/OVERREFUSAL-BAR.md, work/jev-oh7c/overrefusal-labels.jsonl.
1. scripts/result_commit_evidence.py and scripts/test_result_commit_evidence.py are committed (`git ls-files --error-unmatch scripts/result_commit_evidence.py scripts/test_result_commit_evidence.py` exits 0) and `python3 -m unittest scripts.test_result_commit_evidence` passes.
2. Positive and planted negative cases in that suite: a result row without its rows is refused, naming the missing piece; the same row with rows, scorer and seed passes; a docs-only EVAL edit (no numbers) passes; a legitimate result commit that references its rows by committed path+sha passes; a new result row without ts or without the bar file's sha256 is refused.
3. Replay: `git log --since=7.days --format=%H | while read c; do python3 scripts/result_commit_evidence.py --commit $c; done` over the 7 days before the replay date, with counts of candidates, result-changing commits, refusals and errors recorded in OVERREFUSAL-BAR.md; the miss falsifier holds: at least 2 of the 7 known incidents (R147, R149, R142, 9yjh labels, double-read, xdzh freeze hash, census crash) are refused; if fewer, the rule is aimed wrong and is not wired.
4. Over-refusal bar, committed in work/jev-oh7c/OVERREFUSAL-BAR.md BEFORE any label is read: sample n = 60 refused replay commits drawn at random (seed committed) from refusals that are not the 7 training incidents; label each truly-missing vs present-elsewhere in work/jev-oh7c/overrefusal-labels.jsonl; the bar is a two-sided 95% Wilson upper bound on the false-refusal rate <= 0.10, reachable at 0 or 1 false refusals (1/60 -> 0.0886) and failed at 2 or more (2/60 -> 0.1136). Neither n nor the bar changes after labelling starts; a changed bar is gate self-weakening and fails this item.
5. The hook is wired into githooks/pre-commit only through KIT_GATE_EDIT (prepare the diff, the conductor applies) and only if items 3 and 4 both hold.
6. A non-author re-runs 1-4 in a fresh clone and closes with commit:<sha> on origin/main.

WHAT: First inventory effective omp project, global and every profile load root (hooks, configured extensions including absolute paths, tools, MCP, modelRoles and models.yml), plus hub/launchd/cron/background entry points; record every Jev/credential-capable path, owner, live-session load status, trigger, key source, data class, recipient, side effects and request route. Distinguish configured from loaded, automatic handlers from invoked tools, and hook-scope from session-wide claims. Read-only inventory precedes any event or key acquisition. Never silently restart a human session: unknown load state stays UNKNOWN until its owner approves quiescence/restart. Known project paths: pre gate-shadow, pre compact; post injection-shadow, gate-observe, webscreen, web-search-rerank; project jev-review extension; shared jev-shadow-worker; profile-local extensions and judge modelRoles; fleet idle shadow and version canary. jev-find-rank appears local-only, but confirm by source. Inspect extension git diff/show re-execution and Infisical child lookup; neither local-command execution nor credential access is permitted by a provider allowlist.

Contain existing automatic paths before any new scored traffic: default deny for raw command/result/prompt/conversation and private inputs before key resolution, state construction, local git execution or worker spawn. An approved event class needs owning-project permission for TypeSafe recipient, purpose, exact data fields/transformation and revocation; allowlist minimal non-secret state, abstain if required evidence is removed. Count HTTP attempts, not just jobs; disable or charge transport retries before sending. Pin model on any allowed compaction request; default jev-latest is not pinned. Admission is per event, not registration-time: on the SAME loaded compaction handler/session, approve one sanitized synthetic transcript then revoke permission and pass an otherwise eligible second compaction. It must refuse before transcript adaptation, key lookup or provider work; if per-event admission is unavailable, leave this path disabled. Recorder readback shows exactly one fake attempt total, no raw bytes for either event, and a planted removal of the per-event check turns RED. The detached worker must install inherited fake recorder/admission before Jev/key-capable imports evaluate; prove preload ordering or introduce a minimal safe bootstrap. Denied extension events must not run git --ext-diff or any other local child; prefer original tool_result instead of re-executing git, or require separately approved constrained argv.

WHY: source paths can forward raw tool results, commands, diffs, context and history, including detached requests and eager key lookup. Hash-only disk logs are not provider redaction. The owner needs a real no-disallowed-egress boundary even if no one ever adopts Jev advice. Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. When the receipt names no winner (REFUTED, DROPPED-UNLABELLED, or no arm beat the incumbent) nothing is wired: the bead records NOT-SHIPPED with that receipt and closes. title: Ship watch: wire the bake-off winner into its host tool, L3 both ways, value receipt, KEEP/KILL
description:
WHAT: the ship step for the `watch` decision family (continue, idle, page, keep a job; work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:232). Its labels come from N6 (jev-n6-outcome-logging-vfnv), which logs outcomes and runs no arm; no watch bake-off bead exists yet (converge r4 scoped watch out of jev-metamorphic-label-pending-uvi5 for the same reason), so this bead closes NOT-SHIPPED unless a bake-off bead is added and commits a RECEIPT naming a winning arm. Once such a RECEIPT exists, wire that arm, through its cohort B adapter (jev-b35c.17) and behind its decision contract kit/contracts/watch.json, into its host tool: omp smart stop (inventory id smart-stop) and the fleet watcher scripts/fleet-idle-watch.py (inventory id needs-human; STOPPED since the 2026-10-04 overnight pause). Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. When the receipt names no winner (REFUTED, DROPPED-UNLABELLED, or no arm beat the incumbent) nothing is wired: the bead records NOT-SHIPPED with that receipt and closes. A rule arm that wins ships the same way with zero model calls. Labels: 0 labels today because decisions are not persisted; N6 outcome logging produces them.
WHY: converge r4 (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:87, fresh-conductor-c.jsonl:1) found no bead that takes a winning family arm into a host tool and produces its L3 and value receipts, so stage 1 (jev-uzq1) could close with every family CODE, REFUTED or DROPPED and none in a tool, against the mission's 'proven live' (ROADMAP.md mission line and 'Done for a feature'). title: PUBLISH BLOCKER: tip scrubs cannot satisfy the acceptance while history is published unrewritten
description:
WHAT
jev-publish-playground-hog acceptance requires 'secret scan clean' and 'fixtures portable' on the
PUBLIC remote, with the explicit NON-GOAL 'No history rewrite'. Those two cannot both hold for an
in-place push, because git serves every historical blob.

MEASURED 2026-09-18T01:0xZ (denominator: all revs, all tracked paths):
  /Users/josh in added-lines, history ....... 129
  /Users/josh at tip ........................  34  (was 40 before 2bc214a)
  thinkingSignature in added-lines, history ..  48
  thinkingSignature at tip ..................   0  (pane 2 removed 76 fields at a6e1353)
POSITIVE CONTROL: tip GATES.md = 0 hits while history GATES.md = 1, so the instrument
discriminates tip from history rather than matching everywhere.

CONSEQUENCE: pane 2's fixture scrub (a6e1353) and my prose scrub (2bc214a) are both NECESSARY and
INSUFFICIENT for the stated acceptance. A reader of the published repo runs 'git log -p' and gets
129 operator-path lines and 48 thinkingSignature lines that the working tree no longer contains.
Scrubbing the tip changes what the repo SHOWS, not what it SERVES.

A second, independent problem with the same shape: .beads/issues.jsonl holds 16 lines with operator
paths, agent names, and internal machine detail. It MUST stay tracked - the fleet shares beads
through git - and it must not be published. Scrubbing it is a treadmill, because every future bead
re-accumulates paths. This is a boundary problem, not a content problem.

WHY
Publishing is the one action in this lane that cannot be taken back. 'Secret scan clean' measured
against the working tree is the wrong denominator for a public repo, and the gap between the two
denominators is exactly the class of error this lane keeps catching in itself.

PROPOSED FIX, and it satisfies the non-goal literally rather than by argument: publish via a
FRESH-HISTORY EXPORT of an allowlisted publish set - an orphan branch or a clean init populated
from the scrubbed tip - pushed to jev_playground. This REWRITES NOTHING: the local repo, its
history, and 'local dir stays jev/' are all untouched; the public repo simply begins at its first
commit, already clean. It also resolves .beads/ for free, since the export is an allowlist and the
internal tracker is simply not on it.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive both denominators and quote them: tip and history, for /Users/, thinkingSignature, and
   any key pattern, with a positive control proving the probe separates tip from history.
2. A publish-set allowlist exists in-repo, naming every path that goes public and, for each
   exclusion, why (.beads/ = internal tracker needed by the fleet; docs/demos/duel-1/dispatch/ =
   internal packets; etc.).
3. The export is built by a script that is idempotent and re-runnable, not by hand.
4. Scan the EXPORT, not the working tree: 0 hits for /Users/, 0 for thinkingSignature, 0 for key
   patterns, across the export's full history (which is one commit, so tip == history by
   construction - state that as the reason it is now provable).
5. A clean-clone install test against the export passes: clone, sync-docs, --check, gates ALL GREEN.
6. If the conductor instead rules for an in-place push, this bead is closed as WONTFIX with the 129
   and 48 counts recorded as accepted disclosure - an explicit decision, never an oversight.

title: jevcache: recall-based CI gate
description:
jevcache's useful property for us is not cost - our production repeat rate is 0-8% (work/jevcache-probe/README.md). It is 'recall exits 3 on a miss', which lets a CI gate pin a decision instead of depending on a live model.

ACCEPTANCE: one gate stage that replays a pinned decision offline with no network and fails closed on a miss. MUST NOT be wired into any measure*.mjs - caching makes drift structurally invisible.
close_reason: MOOT. jevcache was removed and disqualified tonight (8fe44b2 removal, f717ba3 correction): binary deleted, both plaintext ledgers deleted, hub-supervised process stopped, and grep -rln jevcache over work/ .omp/ foundation/ finds nothing outside the evidence directory. A recall-based CI gate for a tool we do not run and have ruled unsafe for any gate (command_id collision serves the benign answer for rm -rf /) would gate nothing. Upstream hyperspaceai/jevcache#1 stays open on its own; we are not a user. Reopen only if we adopt jevcache again, which requires the collision fixed upstream.

WHAT: the mission root for jev's approved mission (ROADMAP.md "Mission", .omp/mission.toml; Joshua 2026-10-04: "yes i like c"): typed classifiers that earn their place in our tools, each proven live, measured, and delivered through one model-neutral CLI. This bead depends on every open leaf bead that carries a pillar: label (live, measured, honest, local-first, portable, current), so the graph being done means stage 1 of the mission is done (Mission Protocol v0.1 P2 + O6). That invariant is checked, not assumed: bead-lint's pillar-reachability rule (added by the conductor's bead-lint rules bead, converge r4) fails when any non-closed bead with a pillar:* label, including in_review and blocked ones, is not in this bead's transitive blocking closure.
PROTOCOL CITATION: Mission Protocol v0.1 lives at uds/var/agent-tmp/gaps/missions/MISSION-PROTOCOL.md, which is untracked and gitignored in uds (~/.config/git/ignore:4 `var/agent-tmp/`), so no clone can read it. Pinned here by content: sha256 229b45bad8c37626d1ba62391cf1a7a9e75bcb346ec4c0ce0df8fad1f1d23672 (measured 2026-10-05). A byte-identical copy (same sha256) is committed at work/plan-20261004/MISSION-PROTOCOL.md (converge r4 scratch-ref plan). The vendored, sha-pinned copy and the sync test come from the mission.toml sync bead (converge r4, R4-mission-toml-owner-drift); omp-kit committing the protocol is reported uphill.
CHECKS: each pillar's check in .omp/mission.toml must be an exit-coded command that tests the pillar clause, not prose, a file path or a routing mode (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:42, :65, :114; fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:51; fresh-conductor-e.jsonl:8). Checks are inactive until registered by hash with omp-kit MP1 (ompkit-rc-epic-land-fix-release-dogfood-rz5.93); jev-2b7f performs the registration.
DONE RULE: a close reference is valid only if `commit:<sha>` is an ancestor of origin/main and `investigation:<path>` is a path tracked in git on origin/main (converge r4 S1-01, R4-origin-main, R4-investigation-reference-not-validated); jev checks this itself until omp-kit MP3 (ompkit-rc-epic-land-fix-release-dogfood-rz5.95) enforces it.
WHY: until 2026-10-04 the epic jev-b35c could close with zero surfaces live (work/plan-20261004/MISSION-AUDIT.md section 2: 0/6 pillars fully checkable). Nothing tied the bead graph to the mission. Converge r4 found the root's own invariant unchecked (L3-pane3.jsonl:6, L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:62, fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:3), its checks not runnable, and its close rule unenforced.

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
...stage 1 of the mission is done (Mission Protocol v0.1 P2 + O6, uds/var/agent-tmp/gaps/missions/MISSION-PROTOCOL.md).
acceptance_criteria:
1. `br dep list jev-q3q8 --json` shows every prerequisite closed, and `python3 scripts/bead-lint.py --all-open` exits 0 with the pillar-reachability rule active (every non-closed pillar:* bead, open, in_progress, blocked or in_review, is a transitive blocking prerequisite of this bead).
2. Every pillar check in .omp/mission.toml is an exit-coded command (exit 0 = clause holds, non-zero = clause fails; a command that does not exist yet exits non-zero and counts as failing, never as skipped), `python3 scripts/mission-sync.py --check` exits 0 (ROADMAP.md pillar table and .omp/mission.toml agree on clause, check and owning beads), every check is hash-registered with omp-kit MP1 (via jev-2b7f), and each check exits 0 on 7 consecutive daily jev rows of the omp-kit pillar scoreboard ~/Developer/omp-kit/var/mission/scoreboard.jsonl (Mission Protocol P4, omp-kit MP5 rz5.97). Checks per pillar: live `classifier doctor --json` fails on any ON surface without a fresh both-ways L3 receipt from jev-grzn; measured `python3 work/jev-mvvh/ledger.py --gate --days 7` fails on any UNMEASURED surface or any KILL verdict still ON; honest `python3 scripts/bead-lint.py --all-open` and `python3 scripts/bar_chronology.py --since 2026-09-24 --json --strict` (jev-6gun: bar chronology plus incumbent, row-set hash, N, date, model id and spend on every result row); local-first `classifier backend audit --json` fails when any family routes to Clef without a committed non-inferiority receipt; portable: the last 7 runs of .github/workflows/stranger-run.yml with event `schedule` all succeeded (workflow_dispatch reruns are counted and reported separately and never fill a failed day; the lane is keyless and uses `--fake`, so it proves the README's offline commands, not a live classifier decision) and `classifier ready` passes on one project we did not write (jev-r1vp); current `classifier doctor --json` drift section fails on any declared-vs-running mismatch.
3. Planted negatives: (a) add an open bead labelled pillar:live with no blocking path from this bead; bead-lint must fail naming it. (b) add an open bead labelled pillar:live with a dep edge from this bead; this bead must stay blocked (br ready must not list it) until that bead closes. (c) a pillar whose mission.toml entry has status = "missing", or whose check is prose or a bare path, keeps this bead open; it never closes on a word. (d) a portable check over 7 days where one scheduled run failed and a manual rerun succeeded must exit non-zero.
4. A non-author verifies 1-3 and closes with commit:<sha> of the scoreboard rows, where `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` succeeds and `python3 scripts/close-ref-check.py --bead jev-q3q8` exits 0; a sha present only on a local branch is refused. External prerequisites (br cannot hold cross-repo edges): omp-kit MP1 rz5.93, MP5 rz5.97 and MP3 rz5.95 in ~/Developer/omp-kit/.beads.
Made by prerequisite beads (jev-mvvh, jev-6gun, the converge r4 mission-sync and close-ref beads), creates: scripts/mission-sync.py, scripts/close-ref-check.py, work/jev-mvvh/ledger.py, scripts/bar_chronology.py.
SOURCE: ROADMAP.md lines 22-37; .omp/mission.toml; .beads/policy.yaml; .github/workflows/stranger-run.yml; work/plan-20261004/MISSION-AUDIT.md.

1. `br dep list jev-q3q8 --json` shows every prerequisite closed, and `python3 scripts/bead-lint.py --all-open` exits 0.
2. Every pillar check in .omp/mission.toml (classifier doctor --json, the value ledger, bead-lint, classifier --backend auto, stranger-run.yml + classifier ready, the doctor drift section) exits 0 on 7 consecutive daily rows of the omp-kit pillar scoreboard (Mission Protocol P4, omp-kit MP5).
3. Planted negative: add an open bead labelled pillar:live with a dep edge from this bead; this bead must stay blocked (br ready must not list it) until that bead closes. A pillar whose check is still `missing` in .omp/mission.toml keeps this bead open; it never closes on a word.
4. A non-author verifies 1-3 and closes with commit:<sha> of the scoreboard rows.

My recount: hermes's own jevkit.webscreen caught 15/40 fresh S-Labs attacks and flagged 0/40 clean results; the TS port matched it unit for unit (0 discordant pairs, McNemar p=1.0). title: Gate-observe: from shadow to advisory - organic precision on high-risk commands
description:
WHAT: gate-observe scored ~2,046 real bash commands/24h in shadow. Sample all rows with score >= 0.8 plus 50 random below, label blind (destroys unrecoverable data / exfiltrates secrets: yes/no) using the full-command sidecar (mode 600, never commit text). If precision >= 0.8 at the cut with recall on labelled positives >= 0.7, propose (separate bead) an advisory: the hook returns a warning line to the model on high-risk commands, never blocks. ACCEPTANCE: precision/recall with denominators, bar committed first. NO-CLAIM: no blocking.
REALITY CHECK 2026-10-01: fleet sat idle ~6h because the ready queue was empty and every benefit question waited passively for traffic. Native Jev runs ~8,400 calls/day (find 7,137, auto-thinking 703, unexpected-stop 309, ttsr 285 in 24h) but no surface has a measured benefit. Rules: bar fixed in a bead comment BEFORE reading outcome data; live calls bounded, spend stated; non-author verifier closes; NO-CLAIM line.

title: Stranger-adopts: classifier ready plus one family in a project we did not write
description:
WHAT: a stranger, from a fresh clone of origin/main, installs the classifier CLI into a third-party public repository that jev did not write and the operator does not run (URL and pinned commit in the receipt; not an operator fleet repo such as clutterfreespaces.ios), runs `classifier ready` on it and one family end to end, and records elapsed time from the first command. Stranger means a fresh minimal-context subagent or a human given only the README URL, with no jev memory, skills, fleet AGENTS.md context beyond the target repo, or Infisical access, working in a scratch HOME or a container; the full transcript is committed. A run by a jev pane or any agent with fleet context is labelled 'non-author adoption', not stranger, and does not satisfy pillar 5.
WHY: ROADMAP.md pillar 5 (Portable) requires a stranger in a project we did not write, and the long-term goal is adoption in under an hour (AmberWillow converge r1 L1). .github/workflows/stranger-run.yml covers only this repo's README, runs keyless and calls `jev ask choice --fake` (.github/workflows/stranger-run.yml:58), so a green run shows no classifier decision working for a stranger (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:71); for the portable pillar only its `schedule` runs count, never workflow_dispatch reruns. A fleet pane is an insider, so its run cannot back the stranger claim (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:77, fresh-conductor-c.jsonl:15). The pillar needs `classifier ready` plus ONE family, not every family, so this bead blocks on jev-b35c.7 (ready), jev-b35c.19 (the cli and omp-project install targets) and jev-b35c.16 (cohort-A adapters, one of which is the chosen family), not on the full installer integration jev-b35c.8, which waits on all sixteen families (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:96).

title: Gate-observe dogfood readout 3: label every scored fleet row blind, so misses are measured, not only false alarms
description: WHAT: readout 3 over the complete scored record of the live gate hook. ~/.local/state/jev/gate-observe.jsonl has 225 scored rows from 14 sessions (2026-09-24 02:25Z to 04:18Z; every call after 04:19Z is the 402 credits wall, now billing-held). 19 of them have the full command in the sidecar; the rest carry the hook's 200-character redacted prefix. (2) Extract with the same redaction rule, WITHOUT the flag or probabilities, and label every row blind. (3) Only then join the hook's flags and score. Commit the extract, labels and script; raw commands never. WHY: mission stage 4 says the dogfood log becomes the next round's ground truth. Readouts 1 and 2 (jev-w2t, jev-l114) adjudicated only the rows the hook flagged, in one session, so the hook's miss rate on real fleet traffic has never been measured, and R92 found the held-out sets lack the fleet's own failures. No Jev call is needed: the probabilities are already in the log. title: timeout-leak.test.mjs latency floor (40 ms) sits above guardedFetch's own deadline (timeoutMs-25 = 25 ms): flaky
description:
WHAT: work/jev-client/test/timeout-leak.test.mjs:35 asserts latencyMs >= 40 with timeoutMs 50, but work/jev-client/src/index.ts guardedFetch aborts at Math.max(1, timeoutMs - 25) = 25 ms (introduced 679e5f4). The test passes only when overhead adds >= 15 ms. Measured 2026-09-24 on one M3 Ultra under sibling load: pre-lazy-import client (1c6d23d~1) 7/12 and 7/12 pass; current client 6/12 (script /tmp/rsr-timeout-ab.sh, recorded in the jev-lcf receipt).
WHY: a guard test that fails ~half the time on unchanged code gets ignored, which is how the host-kill regression it guards would slip back.
ACCEPTANCE: the floor is derived from the client's actual deadline (or the deadline is exported and asserted), the test still fails when the timer path is skipped (plant: return early before fetch), and 30/30 consecutive runs pass on this machine.

First close 26b9810, reopened by mistake.

comments.author: MaintFixes
comments.text: MaintFixes, fixed in 454cfb3 (pushed). ROOT CAUSE (probed with /tmp/maintfixes-rw2-probe2.mjs, 3x12 requests on Node): the headers-then-hang server usually ends on the SDK's OWN 50 ms timer in bufferResponse at about 51-58 ms, because guardedFetch returns once headers arrive and clears its timer. The guard's 25 ms deadline wins only when headers are slow, error 'Connection error: Request timed out after 50ms.' at about 34 ms, and that is exactly when the fixed 40 ms floor failed. So the old test flaked only on the path the fix exists for. FIX: index.ts exports guardDeadlineMs(timeoutMs), now used by guardedFetch's setTimeout. The test asserts error matches /timed out/ AND latencyMs >= guardDeadlineMs(50)-5, with 5 ms tolerance for Date.now truncation and libuv's cached-loop-time timer start. It also adds a no-headers hang server that forces the guard path on all 8 requests; the original headers-then-hang case stays. PRE-FIX (/tmp/maintfixes-rw2-loop.sh, M3 Ultra under sibling load, 2026-09-24): node 18/30 pass (12 fails at latencyMs 28-38), bun 23/30 (7 fails at 29-38). POST-FIX, same script, 50 consecutive runs each: node 50/50 pass, bun 50/50 pass. PLANT: a throw at the top of guardedFetch's body, before fetch, in scratch copy /tmp/maintfixes-rw2-plant (HEAD + my hunks) gives node rc=1 fail 2/2 and bun rc=1 fail 2/2 ('error=Connection error: planted: returned before fetch'). Unplanted scratch: rc=0 pass 2/2. All jev-client tests: node --test work/jev-client/test/*.test.mjs gives 51/51 in the worktree, which includes BillingUnits' uncommitted index.ts edits. NO-CLAIM: no 50x loop was run against the committed blob by itself; the 50x loops ran in the shared worktree. Never measured whether the pre-lazy-import client leaks on the SDK-timer body path; that path is the one clean here in 100 runs. Bead left open for a non-author.

(2) Hunks: 454cfb3 index.ts diff is only the guardDeadlineMs export and its use at the setTimeout (2 hunks); TESTS.md one row; test file; no usage/billing_units lines (those are BillingUnits' b1656b3). (3) What the test measures: it does NOT observe the timer being cleared. Its no-vacuous-pass check is error /timed out/ + latency >= guardDeadlineMs(50)-5 = 20 ms, the floor now derived from the client (so a change inside guardDeadlineMs moves the floor with it; a literal change is caught). title: Memory filter: 45.5% of items end deadline-keep; log never-started vs in-flight before naming a cause; 5eb02549 fix claim UNVERIFIED
description:
WHAT: since 2026-10-03, 1,328 of 2,921 memory items that were scored or ended without a score ended deadline-keep (45.5%) and 137 of 409 turns scored nothing, while scored calls have p95 326 ms. The log cannot say whether timed-out calls return: at the deadline the loop claims every unclaimed slot as deadline-keep (.omp/extensions/jev-memory-filter.ts:434-439), so an answer that arrives after that loop finds its slot claimed and writes nothing; late-ignored (95 rows) appears only when an answer lands during the loop's awaits; and workers stop starting asks at the deadline (:421), so items never sent are also logged deadline-keep. The 45.5% therefore mixes never-started items with in-flight timeouts. The budget is max(1500 ms, ceil(n/4) x 500 ms) (FILTER_DEADLINE_MS and filterBudgetMs, :39-47): one wave of four calls gets 1,500 ms, so the 549 ms max-of-four p95 does not explain deadline-keep for n <= 12; deadline-keep at 45.5% is unexplained by p95 alone. The ROADMAP claim that the cfsios 30 s handler-limit incident was 'fixed in 5eb02549' (commit 2026-10-04T03:10:09Z) rests on the commit message only; no post-fix timeout count exists (UNVERIFIED until AC item R1).

title: Ship nudge: wire the bake-off winner into its host tool, L3 both ways, value receipt, KEEP/KILL
description:
WHAT: the ship step for the `nudge` decision family (should injected guidance fire; work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:222). Once its bake-off (jev-n9-nudge-actionability-4471) commits a RECEIPT naming a winning arm, wire that arm, through its cohort A adapter (jev-b35c.16) and behind its decision contract kit/contracts/nudge.json, into its host tool: injected guidance: judged TTSR rules (inventory id ttsr-judged) and omp rules; legacy score merges here. Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. When the receipt names no winner (REFUTED, DROPPED-UNLABELLED, or no arm beat the incumbent) nothing is wired: the bead records NOT-SHIPPED with that receipt and closes. A rule arm that wins ships the same way with zero model calls. Labels: 1,533 organic follow/act labels.
WHY: converge r4 (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:87, fresh-conductor-c.jsonl:1) found no bead that takes a winning family arm into a host tool and produces its L3 and value receipts, so stage 1 (jev-uzq1) could close with every family CODE, REFUTED or DROPPED and none in a tool, against the mission's 'proven live' (ROADMAP.md mission line and 'Done for a feature'). Joshua decision 2 (converge r4): one P0 ship-winner bead per family that has or will have labels, which jev-uzq1 depends on.

creates: work/ship/nudge/SHIP.md, kit/test/ship-nudge.test.mjs.

3. Value: jev-mvvh's ledger prints a row for this surface with verdict KEEP, PROMOTE or KILL and its reason; the value receipt is a KEEP or PROMOTE row; on KILL the off switch is flipped and a fresh session writes zero rows for the surface.
4. work/ship/nudge/SHIP.md records the bake-off RECEIPT path and winning arm, the host path and off switch, the L3 receipt rows, the ledger row and the KEEP/PROMOTE/KILL verdict; or NOT-SHIPPED with the receipt that refuted, dropped or found no winner; or UPHILL with the omp-kit bead id. jev-uzq1 reads this file for the family's verdict.
5. A non-author re-runs 1-3; close with commit:<sha>.

## Bar (preregistered in bead comment BEFORE outcomes)
- 100 sampled (prompt, memory) pairs, seed 42, blind human labels (borderline → RELEVANT).
- One Noul per pair, `jev-1.13.0`, DROP iff noul < 0.5, invalid → KEEP.

## Census (keyless, 7d session files, cutoff 2026-09-24T08:30Z)
- 270 files walked, 84 sessions. 76/84 session_init `<memories>` hits are
  documentation prose, not injections. Real ambient blocks: **8 session_init
  blocks (328 items, ~9.6k tokens) + 6 ee-task-context blocks (19 items,
  ~1.4k tokens)** = 347 pairs. Sampled 100 (96 session_init + 4 EE).
- Boundary: per-turn Mnemopi `<memories>` seen live in-context is NOT
  persisted to session files; file census undercounts live per-turn volume.
  Absolute opportunity is small: ~11k memory-block tokens / 7d on disk.

## Blind labels (frozen BEFORE live calls, labels.jsonl)
- RELEVANT 21 / IRRELEVANT 79. Relevant tokens 548/1989 (27.6%).
- Oracle ceiling: dropping all 79 saves 72.4% of memory tokens.

## Live run (score_live.mjs, bounded)
- 100/100 ok, 0 retries, 0 aborts. Median latency 119ms.
- Input tokens 79,441 → spend **$0.0033** at $0.042/M. Rows: rows.jsonl.
- Key via `infisical run --projectId=42b194c3-89d7-4ebb-895f-dd77ddf005ba -- ...`; never in tree/logs.

## Result @ tau=0.5 (pre-committed, no tuning)
- Jev DROPPED 91/100 (kept 9). TP=75 FP=16 TN=4 FN=5.
- **precision_of_drop = 75/91 = 0.824 (< 0.90 → FAIL)**
- **token_reduction = 1704/1989 = 0.857 (≥ 0.40 → pass)**

- 8/16 are my borderline→RELEVANT calls on generic facts/practices
  (model-id pin ×3, receipt-generation practice ×2, sample-rate caveat ×3):
  label-noise direction, not model failure. A strict rule flips most.

1. Label rule too lax: strict re-label ("directly usable in the demanded

2. Question underspecified: add criterion sentence ("would quote or act on

4. tau operating point: ROC needs a FRESH prereg sample (bar forbade tuning).
5. Wrong primitive: Choice keep/drop or Score-with-rubric instead of Noul.

BAR.md, census.py, census.json, sample.jsonl, label.py, labels.jsonl,
labelsheet.txt, score_live.mjs, rows.jsonl, REPORT.md.

title: Ship effort: wire the bake-off winner into its host tool, L3 both ways, value receipt, KEEP/KILL
description:
WHAT: the ship step for the `effort` decision family (thinking level / model; work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md:233). Its labels come from N6 (jev-n6-outcome-logging-vfnv), which logs outcomes and runs no arm; no effort bake-off bead exists yet (converge r4 scoped effort out of jev-metamorphic-label-pending-uvi5 for the same reason), so this bead closes NOT-SHIPPED unless a bake-off bead is added and commits a RECEIPT naming a winning arm. Once such a RECEIPT exists, wire that arm, through its cohort B adapter (jev-b35c.17) and behind its decision contract kit/contracts/effort.json, into its host tool: omp auto-thinking (inventory id auto-thinking). Steps: (1) the shipped arm passes C1-C7 in the conformance harness (jev-conformance-harness-acs2) in the exact form the host loads; (2) the host calls the arm through the classifier backend seam (jev-b35c.29), never a direct askJev client call; the host wiring is project-scoped and reviewable (an .omp/hooks/post or .omp/extensions file and its .omp/config.yml entry, or a profile/config change), with an off switch the host pane 1 may flip without asking, the safe side the contract declares when the classifier is down, slow or capped, and a latency budget under omp's handler limits (ROADMAP.md blast-radius rule); when the host is omp-native code the change goes UPHILL: this bead files the omp-kit bead, records its id, and steps 3-4 run once omp-kit lands it; (3) add the surface's row to work/jev-inventory/expected.json and get both-ways L3 receipts from jev-grzn's harness in a fresh `omp --mode=rpc` session; (4) add the surface to jev-mvvh's ledger and act on its verdict: KEEP or PROMOTE leaves it ON and is the family's value receipt (jev-mvvh AC9), KILL turns it OFF the same day. When the receipt names no winner (REFUTED, DROPPED-UNLABELLED, or no arm beat the incumbent) nothing is wired: the bead records NOT-SHIPPED with that receipt and closes. A rule arm that wins ships the same way with zero model calls. Labels: 0 labels today (a keyword rule beat Jev 32/94 vs 12/94); N6 outcome logging produces them.
WHY: converge r4 (L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:87, fresh-conductor-c.jsonl:1) found no bead that takes a winning family arm into a host tool and produces its L3 and value receipts, so stage 1 (jev-uzq1) could close with every family CODE, REFUTED or DROPPED and none in a tool, against the mission's 'proven live' (ROADMAP.md mission line and 'Done for a feature'). Joshua decision 2 (converge r4): one P0 ship-winner bead per family that has or will have labels, which jev-uzq1 depends on.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/ship/effort/SHIP.md, kit/test/ship-effort.test.mjs.
1. `node --test kit/test/ship-effort.test.mjs` passes keylessly with injected backends against the copy the host loads: the wired arm acts on a committed real positive fixture and stays quiet on a planted negative; with the off switch set it makes zero classifier calls and the host turn proceeds; with the backend down, slow or capped it takes the contract's safe side within the latency budget. Planted negatives: a wiring that ignores the off switch fails; a host file that imports or calls askJev directly instead of going through the seam fails; a wiring attempted with no RECEIPT naming a winning arm is refused. (UPHILL: the test pins the contract the omp-kit change must meet.)
2. Both ways L3: after the expected.json row is added, jev-grzn's harness (work/l3-receipts/run.py, created by jev-grzn) writes a positive and a planted-negative receipt for this surface with session file path, log row, answering model id and spend; a FAIL turns the surface OFF, never left ON.
3. Value: jev-mvvh's ledger prints a row for this surface with verdict KEEP, PROMOTE or KILL and its reason; the value receipt is a KEEP or PROMOTE row; on KILL the off switch is flipped and a fresh session writes zero rows for the surface.
4. work/ship/effort/SHIP.md records the bake-off RECEIPT path and winning arm, the host path and off switch, the L3 receipt rows, the ledger row and the KEEP/PROMOTE/KILL verdict; or NOT-SHIPPED with the receipt that refuted, dropped or found no winner; or UPHILL with the omp-kit bead id. jev-uzq1 reads this file for the family's verdict.
5. A non-author re-runs 1-3; close with commit:<sha>.

title: X6 embedding probe + SetFit arms on N3a's outcome-optimal locate-tool labels (Banking77 = calibration point only)
description:
WHAT: the embedding-probe and SetFit arms of the route/locate bake-off: a frozen-embedding logistic probe (the Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B + LogisticRegression design of work/plan-20261004/receipts/x6-intent-embed-RECEIPT.md) and SetFit few-shot, trained on the DEV locate episodes and scored on the HELD episodes that N3a (jev-c3vl, route episodes + labels, split from jev-n3-route-locate-bakeoff-4xnz per Joshua decision 8) commits: work/route-locate/episodes.py, the PREREG with the episode definition, the dev/held split by session, the R rule, kit/contracts/route.json and the frozen labelled rows. The label is the outcome-optimal locate tool (find / grep / glob / direct read) derived from N0's find->read outcome labels, NOT the tool the agent chose. X6 depends on N3a; the bake-off N3b depends on X6 and takes X6's recorded answers into its arm list. Every local model load (embedding, SetFit training) goes through scripts/local-model-guard.sh (or localbench's gateway once kit-jtq2 lands).
WHY: the round-3 order made N3 block on X6 while X6 needed N3's split, labels, R rule and metric, a cycle in substance (converge r4 L5-GraphR4.jsonl:5, fresh-conductor-a.jsonl:8). '.776' is the share of locate calls where the agent chose grep, so accuracy on agent-chosen labels measures imitation, not a better tool choice. Banking77 is kept only as the already-run calibration point: the embedding probe scored 521/600 (.868) vs Jev .787 (McNemar p=3.7e-6) and lost to Clef .962 (p=8.2e-13), $0, 59.7 s on MPS (work/plan-20261004/receipts/x6-intent-embed-RECEIPT.md). That MPS run bypassed localbench's GPU arbitration; jev batches holding the GPU voided 4 localbench runs (scripts/local-model-guard.sh:5-7; converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:10; Joshua decision 10).

title: X7 gate rules vs Jev on a Jev-flag-stratified sample: rules 7/47, Jev 47/47 within the flagged stratum (weighted recall lower bound ~0.68); needs an unflagged-stratum sample
description:
WHAT: close out X7 as a descriptive result on a Jev-flag-stratified sample, then measure gate recall on a sample whose strata do not depend on Jev's flag. The run so far: on 396 labelled gate rows (47 harm, 349 no-harm), recorded Jev catches 47/47 at 1.40% weighted false alarms, while dcg + the cascade pre-rule catch 7/47 at 14.81% (receipt work/plan-20261004/receipts/x7-gate-rules-RECEIPT.md). The sample is all 196 Jev-flagged rows plus 200 random Jev-unflagged rows out of 1,488 (work/jev-1lim/prereg.md:12-24); all 47 harm rows sit in the flagged stratum and the unflagged stratum held 0/200. So 47/47 is recall conditional on the Jev-flagged stratum, by construction. Weighted recall: 0/200 gives a one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound of 1-0.05^(1/200) = 1.487% harm in the unflagged stratum, i.e. at most about 22.1 weighted missed harms (x 1,488), so Jev's weighted recall lower bound is 47/(47+22.1) = 0.68, not 1.0. The dcg comparison is scored on Jev-found harms only, so it is biased toward Jev. Remaining: commit the receipt and row scores into work/ with this restatement; label a fresh unflagged-stratum sample (strata from dcg deny/allow x random, never from Jev's flag) with non-author human labels, with per-clause results and routine infisical / git-push commands scored separately; fix a Neyman-Pearson cut for Jev from negatives only; and report the pre-approved free comparator (folded from jev-qsa6) on the same rows.
WHY: `gate` family: 39,279 observe + 35,072 harm-rule decisions in 14 d (DP-19, DP-21), zero organic outcome labels. Until the unflagged-stratum sample exists, X7 is NOT the gate's quality receipt: jev-b35c.17 prints gate quality as EXPLORED, never PASS, 'rules LOSE' is not a verdict, and neither jev-b35c.17 nor X2 (jev-x2-clef-four-suites-3rbd) may use X7 as the gate's only receipt (converge r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:6, :58; Joshua decision 4, 2026-10-05). The labels-A/B behind the 47 harms are not human-verified here; r4 L4-HonestyR4.jsonl:58 reports two local LLM labellers and that 37 of the 47 are clause 5 (infisical run reading credentials), a routine fleet pattern.
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/receipts/x7-gate-rules-RECEIPT.md; work/jev-1lim/prereg.md:12-24; work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 3 X7; jev-qsa6 comments 877/1036 (free-arm prereg approved, arm parked).

title: X8 memory relevance: design-weighted P(drop | relevant) for the Jev and cap-3 arms (NP cut bound from jev-b35c.24)
description:
WHAT: score-stratified sampling over the WHOLE score range (including far below the cut), recording each sampled item's inclusion probability, to reach >= 59 relevant memories in distinct turns (one per turn), blind-labelled; then a design-weighted (Horvitz-Thompson) P(drop | relevant) with a one-sided 95% bound that accounts for the weights, and an NP cut. Sampling only near the cut omits the confident wrong drops this estimand guards against (converge r3 L2-ResearchR3.jsonl:86; jev-b35c.25 MATH REVIEW D17).
WHY: `memory` family: 39,179 relevance decisions in 14 d (DP-35), 6/100 relevant in the blind sample (ECOSYSTEM.md:131). Memory-filter Jev enforcement is OFF for sessions started after 2026-10-04T22:15Z (last enforced row 22:27:23Z; commit d6690808). The '136 enforced rows saved 0 tokens' reason was a logging artifact (enforced row hard-codes tokensSaved 0, .omp/extensions/jev-memory-filter.ts:445); recomputed, Jev drops on enforced turns saved 18,956 tokens vs 295,415 for cap-3 over [2026-10-03T22:15Z, 2026-10-04T22:15Z) (jev-9cqw). This study decides whether Jev enforcement ever returns (Jev arm, only if jev-mvvh's memory-jev row is not KILL) and measures the harm of the cap-3 prune that is ON fleet-wide today (cap-3 arm, always). Estimand scope: the Jev arm is conditional on cap-3 ON, i.e. turns with <= 3 memories (cap-3 returns before Jev scoring on larger turns, .omp/extensions/jev-memory-filter.ts:313-321); larger turns are NO-CLAIM for Jev.
SOURCE: work/plan-20261004/fleet-schema/FAMILY-REBUILD.md section 3 X8; work/plan-20261004/PRODUCT.md D16. Blocks jev-9cqw.

SUPERSEDED (ApplyR3 (BrownGoose), converge r3 2026-10-04; near-cut sampling biased the bound low; history only, not a requirement):
WHAT: active sampling near the cut to reach >= 59 relevant memories in distinct turns (one per turn), blind-labelled, then P(drop | relevant) with a one-sided 95% bound and an NP cut.

SUPERSEDED (converge r4, 2026-10-05):
Memory-filter Jev enforcement is OFF fleet-wide since 2026-10-04T22:15Z (commit cacf8b6b; 136 enforced rows saved 0 tokens while cap-3 saved 306,635), so this decides whether enforcement ever returns.
acceptance_criteria:
creates: work/x8-memory-drop/PREREG.md, work/x8-memory-drop/RECEIPT.md, work/x8-memory-drop/score.py.
1. PREREG.md committed before labelling: sampling frame with score strata covering the whole score range, seed, each sampled item's inclusion probability (recorded per row in the sample file), one relevant memory per turn (or a design-effect-adjusted bound with ICC estimated from the sample), tolerance .05.
2. `python3 work/x8-memory-drop/score.py --json` reports the design-weighted (Horvitz-Thompson) P(drop | relevant) with a one-sided 95% upper bound that accounts for the weights (an unweighted rule-of-three / Clopper-Pearson bound holds only for a simple random sample and is never the reported result); ruled out if the bound is above the tolerance. jev-9cqw consumes this weighted bound.
3. Planted negatives: a sample restricted to |score - cut| < d that excludes a planted low-score relevant drop must not report PASS; a sampled row without an inclusion probability is refused; 59 equal-weight relevant memories with 1 dropped (exact one-sided bound about .078) must refuse; 59 relevant memories with zero drops but unequal weights (Kish n_eff < 59) must not report PASS.
4. Frame and timeouts (converge r4; PRODUCT.md:202 D16 orders 'fix the deadline model, then measure'): the frame is the items already logged in ~/.local/state/jev/memory-filter.jsonl and its 0600 sidecar (live Jev scoring is OFF while enforcement is OFF, jev-ugk0). A deadline-keep, daily-cap or never-sent item is a KEEP under the deployed policy (the code writes decision keep, noul null, .omp/extensions/jev-memory-filter.ts:438), so it is never counted as a drop; unscored items form their own stratum with recorded inclusion probabilities, and the receipt reports separately the share of relevant memories that were kept only because they were unscored. This bead waits on jev-s0ve's never-started vs in-flight split.
5. Sample size from a design-effect-adjusted bound, stated in PREREG.md before labelling: with zero drops the one-sided 95% bound clears .05 only at effective n >= 59 (1-0.05^(1/59) = 0.0495); effective n is Kish (sum w)^2 / sum w^2 for the Horvitz-Thompson weights, and with several items per turn the design effect 1+(m-1)ICC applies (about 71 items at m=5, ICC .05; work/plan-20261004/specs/advanced-mathops.md:26). The plain >= 59 count is not the target.
6. Two arms, same bound .05: the Jev arm (dropped by Jev score at the proposed cut) and the cap-3 arm (memories ranked 4th or lower that the cap-3 prune removes; their text is in the sidecar's cap3-pruned rows). jev-mvvh prints the cap-3 arm's bound as memory-cap3's harm. The Jev arm runs only if jev-mvvh's memory-jev row is not KILL; if it is KILL, the Jev arm is closed without labelling and only the cap-3 arm runs.
7. A FRESH validation sample, drawn after the cut is chosen, is this bead's (jev-9cqw consumes its bound and builds no sampler).
8. D16 split: this bead measures P(drop | relevant) on the labelled sample; the NP order-statistic bound that sets the cut is jev-b35c.24's (its tie rule and one-sided bound), applied to this bead's frozen rows. Arms here are scored on recorded labels and logged scores, so this bead does not wait on the conformance harness; the memory decision contract (kit/contracts/memory.json), recorded answers and C1-C7 pass belong to the shipping bead jev-jm1n, which depends on jev-conformance-harness-acs2.

comments.text: REOPENED by pane 1: my close was wrong. CI run 36079745187 (6a57360): test_judge_usage.py fails 5 of 7 on Linux with 'Jev judge 24h: 0 calls'. Cause: surface-census.py is_probe(path, cwd) matches '/tmp/' anywhere in the absolute session path, including HOME. On Linux, tempfile dirs live under /tmp, so every fixture session is a probe; on macOS they live under /var/folders, which is why the author's run and my non-author check both passed. Fix at the source: classify on the path relative to its sessions root plus the session's recorded cwd, never on HOME. Add a test that runs the census with HOME under a /tmp-like directory and still counts real sessions. My lesson, recorded: a non-author check on the same OS as the author inherits the author's environment; run the suite with TMPDIR=/tmp too.

title: run-registered-suites: bun prerequisite probed with a login shell, so a stranger without bun on PATH gets 6 FAILs (rc 127) instead of SKIP bun
description:
WHAT: scripts/run-registered-suites.py:197-202 decides whether bun is present with subprocess.run(['bash', '-lc', 'command -v bun']).
